title: حِكَايَةُ الذِّئْبِ وَالثَّعْلَبِ
part: Night 149 · The Wolf and the Fox, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 733–744 (Night 149, continuing directly from nights-148), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 149 carries on the tale of the wolf and the fox who share a den. The fox, smarting from the wolf's blow, swallows his pride and flatters him, but plots his ruin. Finding a gap in a vineyard wall, he looks closer and discovers a pit dug by the owner to trap wild beasts, thinly covered over; he tells the wolf the owner is dead and the vineyard is theirs, and the wolf, blinded by greed, walks onto the cover and falls in. There follows a long exchange of proverbs and verse across the mouth of the pit: the wolf pleads for rescue and promises riches, the fox mocks him, and tells the fable of the falcon who coaxed a partridge from its hole with a promise of grain and ate it. When the wolf weeps and vows to repent, wear wool and live as a hermit, the fox takes pity and dangles his tail into the pit; the wolf pulls him in. Trapped together, the fox talks the wolf into lifting him on his shoulders to the rim, and once out he faints, then laughs: he never meant to save an enemy, and the wolf bites his own hand in remorse as dawn breaks. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ التَّاسِعَةُ وَالْأَرْبَعُونَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-tāsiʿatu wa-al-arbaʿūna baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the ninth-and-forty after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and forty-ninth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الذِّئْبَ قَالَ لِلثَّعْلَبِ لَا تَتَكَلَّمْ فِيمَا لَا يَعْنِيكَ تَسْمَعْ مَالَا يُرْضِيكَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-dhiʾba qāla li-al-thaʿlabi lā tatakallam fīmā lā yaʿnīka tasmaʿ mā lā yurḍīka
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the wolf said to the fox: Do-not speak about what does-not concern-you, (or) you-will-hear what does-not please-you.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the wolf said to the fox, “Do not meddle in what is no concern of yours, or you will hear what you will not like.”
sentences.n: The night opens by repeating the wolf's proverb, where the last night broke off. The fatḥa in بلَغني is the print's own; mālā, run together as مالا, is the print's spacing for mā lā.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الثَّعْلَبُ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً فَأَنَا بِمَعْزِلٍ عَنْ مَالَا يُرْضِيكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-thaʿlabu samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan fa-anā bi-maʿzilin ʿan mā lā yurḍīka
sentences.l: And the fox said to him: Hearing and obedience! For I (am) in-a-place-apart from what does-not please-you.
sentences.i: The fox answered, “With hearing and obedience: I keep well clear of anything that displeases you.”
sentences.n: samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan, accusatives of an unspoken verb: “(I give) hearing and obedience”, the stock reply of a subordinate. bi-maʿzil ʿan, “aloof from, having nothing to do with”, from ʿazala, “to set apart”.

sentences.t: فَقَدْ قَالَ الْحَكِيمُ لَا تَقُولَنَّ عَنْ مَالَا تُسْأَلُ عَنْهُ وَلَا تُجِبْ مَالَا تُدْعَى إِلَيْهِ وَذَرِ الَّذِي لَا يَعْنِيكَ إِلَى مَا يَعْنِيكَ وَلَا تَبْذُلَنَّ النَّصِيحَةَ لِلْأَشْرَارِ فَإِنَّهُمْ يُجَازُونَكَ عَلَيْهَا شَرًّا
sentences.tr: fa-qad qāla al-ḥakīmu lā taqūlanna ʿan mā lā tusʾalu ʿanhu wa-lā tujib mā lā tudʿā ilayhi wa-dhari alladhī lā yaʿnīka ilā mā yaʿnīka wa-lā tabdhulanna al-naṣīḥata li-al-ashrāri fa-innahum yujāzūnaka ʿalayhā sharran
sentences.l: For the sage has said: Do-not speak-indeed about what you-are-not asked about, and do-not answer what you-are-not called to, and leave that-which does-not concern-you for what concerns-you, and do-not lavish-indeed the counsel on the wicked, for they repay-you for-it (with) evil.
sentences.i: For the sage has said: Never speak of what you are not asked about, nor answer what you are not called upon to answer; leave what is none of your business for what is; and never waste good counsel on the wicked, for they will repay you for it with harm.
sentences.n: taqūlanna and tabdhulanna carry the energetic -anna, which strengthens a prohibition: “never …!”. dhar, “leave!”, is an imperative used only in this form; its kasra here (وذَرِ) is the print's own, a helping vowel before the next word, as are the marks in تُجِب and the shadda in شرّا. yujāzūnaka ʿalayhā sharran, “they requite you for it with evil”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الثَّعْلَبُ كَلَامَ الذِّئْبِ تَبَسَّمَ فِي وَجْهِهِ وَلَكِنَّهُ أَضْمَرَ لَهُ مَكْرًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-thaʿlabu kalāma al-dhiʾbi tabassama fī wajhihi wa-lākinnahu aḍmara lahu makran
sentences.l: And when the fox heard the speech of the wolf, he smiled in his face, but he concealed for him a guile,
sentences.i: When the fox heard what the wolf said, he smiled in his face, but in his heart he plotted a trick against him,
sentences.n: aḍmara, “to hide in one's heart, harbour (a design)”. makr, “cunning, a ruse”.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَابُدَّ أَنْ أَسْعَى وَأَكُونَ سَبَبًا لِهَلَاكِ هَذَا الذِّئْبِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lā budda an asʿā wa-akūna sababan li-halāki hādhā al-dhiʾbi
sentences.l: and said: There-is-no escape (but) that I strive and be a cause for the perishing of this wolf.
sentences.i: and said to himself, “I must set to work and be the cause of this wolf's destruction.”
sentences.n: lā budda an, “it is unavoidable that, I must”: the print runs it together as لابد. saʿā, “to strive, exert oneself”.

sentences.t: وَصَبَرَ عَلَى أَذَى الذِّئْبِ وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ إِنَّ الْبَطَرَ وَالِافْتِرَاءَ يَكُونَانِ سَبَبًا لِلْهَلَاكِ وَيُوقِعَانِ فِى الِارْتِبَاكِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣabara ʿalā adhā al-dhiʾbi wa-qāla fī nafsihi inna al-baṭara wa-al-iftirāʾa yakūnāni sababan li-al-halāki wa-yūqiʿāni fī al-irtibāki
sentences.l: And he endured the harm of the wolf, and said in himself: Indeed the insolence and the slander are a cause for the perishing, and they cast into the entanglement.
sentences.i: He bore the wolf's ill-treatment patiently, saying to himself, “Insolence and slander bring about ruin and land one in a snare.”
sentences.n: baṭar, “arrogance, insolence of prosperity”; iftirāʾ, “false accusation, slander”, here rather the wolf's overbearing injustice. halāk and irtibāk rhyme. فى, with ى, is the print's usual spelling of fī.

sentences.t: فَقَدْ قِيلَ مَنْ بَطِرَ خَسِرَ وَمَنْ جَهِلَ نَدِمَ وَمَنْ خَافَ سَلِمَ وَالْإِنْصَافُ مِنْ شِيَمِ الْأَشْرَافِ وَالْآدَابُ أَشْرَفُ الِاكْتِسَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-qad qīla man baṭira khasira wa-man jahila nadima wa-man khāfa salima wa-al-inṣāfu min shiyami al-ashrāfi wa-al-ādābu ashrafu al-iktisābi
sentences.l: For it has been said: Who is-insolent, loses; and who is-ignorant, regrets; and who fears, is-safe; and the fairness (is) from the traits of the noble, and the good-manners (are) the noblest of the acquiring.
sentences.i: For it is said: The insolent man loses, the ignorant man repents, and the fearful man comes off safe; fair dealing is the mark of the noble, and good breeding is the noblest of acquisitions.
sentences.n: A string of maxims in rhymed prose: three short conditionals (man …, “whoever …”), then ashrāf/iktisāb. shiyam, plural of shīma, “natural disposition, trait”. ādāb, plural of adab, “good manners, cultivation”.

sentences.t: وَمِنَ الرَّأْيِ مُدَارَاةُ هَذَا الْبَاغِي وَلَابُدَّ لَهُ مِنْ مَصْرَعٍ
sentences.tr: wa-mina al-raʾyi mudārātu hādhā al-bāghī wa-lā budda lahu min maṣraʿin
sentences.l: And from the (sound) judgement (is) the humouring of this oppressor, and there-is-no escape for-him from a downfall.
sentences.i: Good sense lies in humouring this tyrant; and he is bound to come to a fall.
sentences.n: mudārāh, “humouring, handling with tact”: the fox's policy from here on. bāghī, “one who transgresses, an oppressor”. maṣraʿ, “place or moment of being thrown down”, often “violent death”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الثَّعْلَبَ قَالَ لَهُ إِنَّ الرَّبَّ يَغْفِرُ لِلْعَبْدِ الْمُذْنِبِ وَيَتُوبُ عَلَى عَبْدِهِ اِنْ اقْتَرَفَ الذُّنُوبَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-thaʿlaba qāla lahu inna al-rabba yaghfiru li-al-ʿabdi al-mudhnibi wa-yatūbu ʿalā ʿabdihi in iqtarafa al-dhunūba
sentences.l: Then the fox said to him: Indeed the Lord forgives the sinning servant, and turns (in mercy) upon His servant if he has-committed the sins.
sentences.i: Then the fox said to him, “The Lord forgives His servant who sins, and relents towards him if he has committed sins.
sentences.n: tāba ʿalā, said of God, “to relent towards, accept the repentance of”. iqtarafa, “to commit (a sin)”. The kasra and sukūn in اِنْ are the print's own.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا عَبْدٌ ضَعِيفٌ وَقَدِ ارْتَكَبْتُ فِي نُصْحِكَ التَّعْمِيفَ
sentences.tr: wa-anā ʿabdun ḍaʿīfun wa-qadi irtakabtu fī nuṣḥika al-taʿmīfa
sentences.l: And I (am) a weak servant, and I have committed in my-advising-you the harshness(?).
sentences.i: I am a feeble servant, and in counselling you I was guilty of harshness.
sentences.n: The print has التعميف, which is not a known word. Most likely it is a slip for التعنيف, al-taʿnīf, “harsh reproach, roughness”, which fits the sense and rhymes with ḍaʿīf; the rendering follows that reading. nuṣḥika, “my advising you”: the -ka is the object of the verbal noun.

sentences.t: وَلَوْ عَلِمْتَ بِمَا حَصَلَ لِي مِنْ أَلَمِ لَطْمَتِكَ لَعَلِمْتَ أَنَّ الْفِيلَ لَا يَقُومُ بِهِ وَلَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-law ʿalimta bi-mā ḥaṣala lī min alami laṭmatika la-ʿalimta anna al-fīla lā yaqūmu bihi wa-lā yaqdiru ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And if you-knew of what befell me from the pain of your-slap, you-would-know that the elephant could-not stand-up under-it nor be-capable of-it.
sentences.i: If you knew what pain your blow gave me, you would know that not even an elephant could bear it or endure it.
sentences.n: law … la-, “if … then (would)”. qāma bi-, “to bear, carry (a load)”. The fatḥa in علمتَ is the print's own, fixing “you knew”.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنِّي لَا أَشْتَكِي مِنْ أَلَمِ هَذِهِ اللَّطْمَةِ بِسَبَبِ مَاحَصَلَ لِي بِهَا مِنَ السُّرُورِ
sentences.tr: wa-lākinnī lā ashtakī min alami hādhihi al-laṭmati bi-sababi mā ḥaṣala lī bihā mina al-surūri
sentences.l: But I do-not complain of the pain of this slap, because-of what befell me by-it of the joy.
sentences.i: Yet I do not complain of the pain of this blow, because of the joy it has brought me.
sentences.n: The print runs mā ḥaṣala together as ماحصل.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهَا وَإِنْ كَانَتْ قَدْ بَلَغَتْ مِنِّي مَبْلَغًا عَظِيمًا عَاقِبَتُهَا سُرُورٌ
sentences.tr: fa-innahā wa-in kānat qad balaghat minnī mablaghan ʿaẓīman ʿāqibatuhā surūrun
sentences.l: For it, even-if it had reached from-me a great reaching, its outcome (is) joy.
sentences.i: For though it struck me to the quick, its outcome is happiness.
sentences.n: balagha minhu mablaghan, “to affect someone deeply”, with the verbal noun mablagh strengthening the verb. wa-in, “even if”.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قَالَ الْحَكِيمُ ضَرْبُ الْمُؤَدِّبِ أَوَّلُهُ صَعْبٌ شَدِيدٌ وَآخِرُهُ أَحْلَى مِنَ الْعَسَلِ الْمُصَفَّى
sentences.tr: wa-qad qāla al-ḥakīmu ḍarbu al-muʾaddibi awwaluhu ṣaʿbun shadīdun wa-ākhiruhu aḥlā mina al-ʿasali al-muṣaffā
sentences.l: And the sage has said: The beating of the teacher, its first (is) hard, severe, and its last (is) sweeter than the clarified honey.
sentences.i: The sage has said: A tutor's beating is hard and harsh at first, but in the end it is sweeter than strained honey.”
sentences.n: muʾaddib, “one who teaches manners, a tutor”, from the same root as adab. al-ʿasal al-muṣaffā, “purified honey”, a Qurʾānic phrase (47:15).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الذِّئْبُ قَدْ غَفَرْتُ ذَنْبَكَ وَأَقَلْتُ عَثْرَتَكَ فَكُنْ مِنْ قُوَّتِي عَلَي حَذَرٍ وَاعْتَرِفْ لِي بِالْعُبُودِيَّةِ فَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ قَهْرِي لِمَنْ عَادَانِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-dhiʾbu qad ghafartu dhanbaka wa-aqaltu ʿathrataka fa-kun min quwwatī ʿalā ḥadharin wa-iʿtarif lī bi-al-ʿubūdiyyati fa-qad ʿalimta qahrī li-man ʿādānī
sentences.l: And the wolf said: I have forgiven your sin and overlooked your stumble; so be of my strength on guard, and acknowledge to me the servitude, for you-have-known my subduing of whoever is-hostile-to-me.
sentences.i: The wolf said, “I have forgiven your offence and pardoned your slip. So be wary of my strength, and own yourself my slave; for you know how I crush any who oppose me.”
sentences.n: aqāla ʿathratahu, “to pardon someone's stumble, overlook a lapse”. kun ʿalā ḥadharin min, “be on your guard against”; the print spells ʿalā here as علي, with dotted ي. iʿtarafa bi-, “to acknowledge, confess”: bi- marks what is acknowledged.

sentences.t: فَسَجَدَ لَهُ الثَّعْلَبُ وَقَالَ لَهُ أَطَالَ اللَّهُ عُمْرَكَ وَلَازِلْتَ قَاهِرًا لِمَنْ عَادَاكَ
sentences.tr: fa-sajada lahu al-thaʿlabu wa-qāla lahu aṭāla allāhu ʿumraka wa-lā zilta qāhiran li-man ʿādāka
sentences.l: And the fox prostrated to him and said to him: May God lengthen your life, and may-you-not cease (being) subduer of whoever is-hostile-to-you.
sentences.i: The fox bowed down before him and said, “May God lengthen your days, and may you ever triumph over your enemies!”
sentences.n: Past-tense verbs as wishes: aṭāla allāhu, “may God lengthen”; lā zilta, “may you not cease”, that is, “may you always be”. The print runs lā zilta together as لازلت.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلِ الثَّعْلَبُ خَائِفًا مِنَ الذِّئْبِ مُدَارِيًا مُصَانِعًا لَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazali al-thaʿlabu khāʾifan mina al-dhiʾbi mudāriyan muṣāniʿan lahu
sentences.l: And the fox did-not cease (being) afraid of the wolf, humouring, flattering him.
sentences.i: And the fox remained in fear of the wolf, humouring him and flattering him.
sentences.n: lam yazal, “did not cease”, takes a predicate in the accusative: “remained …”. muṣāniʿ, “one who flatters, cajoles”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الثَّعْلَبَ أَتَى إِلَى الْكَرْمِ يَوْمًا فَرَأَي فِي حَائِطِهِ ثُلْمَةً فَأَنْكَرَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-thaʿlaba atā ilā al-karmi yawman fa-raʾā fī ḥāʾiṭihi thulmatan fa-ankarahā
sentences.l: Then the fox came to the vineyard one day, and saw in its wall a breach, and found-it-strange.
sentences.i: One day the fox came to the vineyard and saw a gap in its wall, which struck him as strange.
sentences.n: karm, “vine, vineyard”. thulma, “breach, gap”. ankara, “to find strange, be suspicious of”. The print spells raʾā here as رأي, with dotted ي.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ إِنَّ هَذِهِ الثُّلْمَةَ لَا بُدَّ لَهَا مِنْ سَبَبٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla fī nafsihi inna hādhihi al-thulmata lā budda lahā min sababin
sentences.l: And he said in himself: Indeed this breach, there-is-no escape for-it from a cause.
sentences.i: He said to himself, “There must be some reason for this gap.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قِيلَ فِى الْمَثَلِ مَنْ رَأَى خَرْقًا فِى الْأَرْضِ فَلَمْ يَجْتَنِبْهُ وَيَتَوَقَّى عَنِ الْإِقْدَامِ عَلَيْهِ كَانَ بِنَفْسِهِ مَغْرُورًا وَلِلْهَلَاكِ مُتَعَرِّضًا
sentences.tr: wa-qad qīla fī al-mathali man raʾā kharqan fī al-arḍi fa-lam yajtanibhu wa-yatawaqqā ʿani al-iqdāmi ʿalayhi kāna bi-nafsihi maghrūran wa-li-al-halāki mutaʿarriḍan
sentences.l: And it has been said in the proverb: Whoever sees a hole in the ground and does-not avoid-it and guard against the venturing upon-it, is about himself deceived, and to the perishing exposed.
sentences.i: It is said in the proverb: Whoever sees a hole in the ground and does not keep clear of it, and beware of setting foot on it, is deluded about himself and courts destruction.
sentences.n: The print has تيل, a misprint for قيل, corrected here. yatawaqqā keeps its final ى after lam, where Classical grammar would shorten it to the jussive yatawaqqa; the print often lets a second verb slip back to the indicative like this. tawaqqā ʿan, “to guard oneself against”; iqdām ʿalā, “venturing upon”. maghrūr, “deceived, deluded”; mutaʿarriḍ li-, “exposing oneself to”.

sentences.t: وَقَدِ اشْتَهَرَ أَنَّ بَعْضَ النَّاسِ يَعْمَلُ صُورَةَ الثَّعْلَبِ فِى الْكَرْمِ حَتَّى يُقَدِّمَ إِلَيْهِ الْعِنَبَ فِى الْأَطْبَاقِ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ يَرَي ذَلِكَ ثَعْلَبٌ فَيَقْدَمَ إِلَيْهِ فَيَقَعَ فِى الْهَلَاكِ
sentences.tr: wa-qadi ishtahara anna baʿḍa al-nāsi yaʿmalu ṣūrata al-thaʿlabi fī al-karmi ḥattā yuqaddima ilayhi al-ʿinaba fī al-aṭbāqi li-ajli an yarā dhālika thaʿlabun fa-yaqdama ilayhi fa-yaqaʿa fī al-halāki
sentences.l: And it has become-well-known that some of the people make the image of the fox in the vineyard, so-that he puts-before it the grapes in the dishes, for-the-sake-of that a fox see that and come to it and fall into the perishing.
sentences.i: And it is well known that some people set up the figure of a fox in a vineyard and even lay grapes before it on platters, so that a fox may see it, come up to it, and fall to his ruin.
sentences.n: A decoy: the painted or modelled fox, apparently feasting, draws the real one in. ḥattā here is “so that, even to the point of”. The print spells yarā as يري, with dotted ي.

sentences.t: وَإِنِّي أَرَى هَذِهِ الثُّلْمَةَ مَكِيدَةً
sentences.tr: wa-innī arā hādhihi al-thulmata makīdatan
sentences.l: And I see this breach (as) a trap.
sentences.i: I take this gap for a snare.
sentences.n: makīda, “a plot, stratagem, trap”, from kāda, “to scheme”.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قِيلَ فِى الْمَثَلِ الْحَذَرُ نِصْفُ الشَّطَارَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad qīla fī al-mathali al-ḥadharu niṣfu al-shaṭārati
sentences.l: And it has been said in the proverb: The caution (is) half of the cleverness.
sentences.i: As the proverb has it, caution is half of cunning.
sentences.n: The print has المتل, a misprint for المثل, corrected here. shaṭāra, “cleverness, smartness, roguish cunning”; the shāṭir is the clever rogue of popular tales.

sentences.t: وَمِنَ الْحَذَرِ أَنْ أَبْحَثَ هَذِهِ الثُّلْمَةَ وَأَنْظُرَ لَعَلِّي أَجِدُ عِنْدَهَا مَكِيدَةً تُؤَدِّي إِلَى التَّلَفِ
sentences.tr: wa-mina al-ḥadhari an abḥatha hādhihi al-thulmata wa-anẓura laʿallī ajidu ʿindahā makīdatan tuʾaddī ilā al-talafi
sentences.l: And from the caution (is) that I examine this breach and look; perhaps I find at-it a trap that leads to the destruction.
sentences.i: It is part of caution to examine this gap and look about; perhaps I shall find some trap here that leads to ruin.
sentences.n: baḥatha, “to search, examine”, here with a direct object. The shadda in لعلّي is the print's own.

sentences.t: وَلَا يَحْمِلُنِى الطَّمَعُ عَلَى أَنْ أُلْقِيَ نَفْسِي فِى الْهَلَكَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā yaḥmilunī al-ṭamaʿu ʿalā an ulqiya nafsī fī al-halakati
sentences.l: And the greed shall-not carry me on to that I cast myself into the perdition.
sentences.i: Greed shall not drive me to throw myself into destruction.”
sentences.n: ḥamalahu ʿalā, “to induce, drive someone to”. A Qurʾānic echo: wa-lā tulqū bi-aydīkum ilā al-tahluka, “do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction” (2:195).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَنَا مِنْهَا وَطَافَ بِهَا وَهُوَ مُحَاذِرٌ وَتَأَمَّلَهَا فَإِذَا هِيَ حَفِيرَةٌ عَظِيمَةٌ قَدْ حَفَرَهَا صَاحِبُ الْكَرْمِ لِيَصِيدَ فِيهَا الْوَحْشَ الَّذِي يُفْسِدُ الْكَرْمَ
sentences.tr: thumma danā minhā wa-ṭāfa bihā wa-huwa muḥādhirun wa-taʾammalahā fa-idhā hiya ḥafīratun ʿaẓīmatun qad ḥafarahā ṣāḥibu al-karmi li-yaṣīda fīhā al-waḥsha alladhī yufsidu al-karma
sentences.l: Then he drew-near to-it and went-round about-it while he (was) wary, and he scrutinised-it, and behold, it (was) a great pit which the owner of the vineyard had dug to catch in-it the wild-beast that spoils the vineyard.
sentences.i: Then he drew near it and circled round it warily, and looked it over closely; and behold, it was a great pit that the owner of the vineyard had dug to trap the wild beast that was ravaging his vines.
sentences.n: fa-idhā, “and behold”, introduces the discovery. ṭāfa bi-, “to go round (something)”. waḥsh, “wild beast(s)”, often collective.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِنَفْسِهِ إِنَّكَ نِلْتَهُ مَا أَمَلّتَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla li-nafsihi innaka niltahu mā ammaltahu
sentences.l: And he said to himself: Indeed you have-attained-it, what you-hoped-for(?).
sentences.i: And he said to himself, “You have got what you hoped for!”
sentences.n: A doubtful phrase. The print has انك نلته ما املّته, with an extra -hu on nilta and the shadda set on the lām of املّته. The likeliest reading is innaka nilta mā ammaltahu, “you have attained what you hoped for”: his caution has paid off. The print's shadda is kept where it stands; ammala, “to hope for”, properly has it on the mīm.

sentences.t: وَرَأَى عَلَيْهَا غِطَاءً نَحِيفًا رَقِيقًا فَتَأَخَّرَ عَنْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-raʾā ʿalayhā ghiṭāʾan naḥīfan raqīqan fa-taʾakhkhara ʿanhā
sentences.l: And he saw on-it a thin, flimsy covering, so he drew-back from-it
sentences.i: He saw a thin, flimsy covering over it, and backed away from it,
sentences.n: The shadda in فتأخّر is the print's own.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ حَيْثُ حَذِرْتُهَا وَأَرْجُوأَنْ يَقَعَ فِيهَا عَدُوِّي الذِّئْبُ الَّذِي نَغَّصَ عَيْشِي فَيَخْلُوَلِي الْكَرْمُ وَأَسْتَقِلَّ بِهِ وَحْدِى وَأَعِيشَ فِيهِ آمِنًا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla al-ḥamdu li-allāhi ḥaythu ḥadhirtuhā wa-arjū an yaqaʿa fīhā ʿaduwwī al-dhiʾbu alladhī naghghaṣa ʿayshī fa-yakhluwa lī al-karmu wa-astaqilla bihi waḥdī wa-aʿīsha fīhi āminan
sentences.l: And he said: The praise (be) to God, in-that I-was-wary-of-it; and I-hope that there-fall into-it my enemy the wolf who troubled my life, so the vineyard be-empty for-me, and I-have it to-myself alone, and I-live in-it safe.
sentences.i: and said, “Praise be to God that I was on my guard against it! And I hope my enemy the wolf, who has soured my life, will fall into it; then the vineyard will be left to me, I shall have it all to myself, and live in it in safety.”
sentences.n: The print runs several words together here: وارجوان for wa-arjū an, فيخلولي for fa-yakhluwa lī; the spacing is kept. ḥaythu, “where”, is used loosely as “in that, since”, a common Middle Arabic habit. naghghaṣa ʿayshahu, “to embitter someone's life”. istaqalla bi-, “to have something to oneself”; the shadda in واستقلّ is the print's own. وحدى is the print's spelling of waḥdī, with ى.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ هَزَّ رَأْسَهُ وَضَحِكَ ضَحِكًا عَالِيًا وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: thumma hazza raʾsahu wa-ḍaḥika ḍaḥikan ʿāliyan wa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: Then he shook his head and laughed a loud laughing, and recited, saying:
sentences.i: Then he shook his head, laughed aloud, and recited:
sentences.n: anshada yaqūlu, “he recited, saying”, the stock formula that brings in verse.

sentences.t:
لَيْتَنِي اَبْصَرْتُ هَذَا الْوَقْتَ * فِي ذِى الْبِئْرِ ذِئْبَا
طَالَ مَاقَدْ سَاءَ قَلْبِي * وَسَقَانِى الْمُرَّ غَصْبَا
لَيْتَنِي مِنْ بَعْدِ هَذَا * اَبْقَى وَيَقْضِى الذِّئْبُ نَحْبَا
ثُمَّ يَخْلُوْ الْكَرْمُ مِنْهُ * وَاَرَى لِي فِيهِ نَهْبَا
sentences.tr:
laytanī abṣartu hādhā al-waqta * fī dhī al-biʾri dhiʾbā
ṭāla mā qad sāʾa qalbī * wa-saqānī al-murra ghaṣbā
laytanī min baʿdi hādhā * abqā wa-yaqḍī al-dhiʾbu naḥbā
thumma yakhlū al-karmu minhu * wa-arā lī fīhi nahbā
sentences.l:
Would-that-I saw at this time * in this pit a wolf!
Long has-it-been that he grieved my heart * and gave-me-to-drink the bitter by-force.
Would-that-I after this * remain, and the wolf fulfil (his) term,
Then the vineyard be-empty of-him * and I see for me in-it plunder!
sentences.i:
Would that I might see, this very hour, * a wolf down in this pit!
Long has he grieved my heart * and forced me to drink bitter draughts.
Would that after this I might live on, * and the wolf meet his end;
then the vineyard would be rid of him, * and I should find my spoils in it.
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own. dhī, “this”, is the feminine demonstrative, agreeing with biʾr, “well, pit”, which is feminine. ṭāla mā, “long has it been that”, run together in the print as ماقد. qaḍā naḥbahu, literally “he fulfilled his vow”, means “he died”, after Qurʾān 33:23; here the possessive is dropped for the rhyme. Every line ends in -bā, the lengthened accusative ending used for rhyme.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ انْطَلَقَ مُسْرِعًا حَتَّى أَتَى إِلَى الذِّئْبِ وَقَالَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَهَّلَ لَكَ الْأُمُورَ إِلَى الْكَرْمِ بِلَاتَعَبٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi inṭalaqa musriʿan ḥattā atā ilā al-dhiʾbi wa-qāla inna allāha sahhala laka al-umūra ilā al-karmi bi-lā taʿabin
sentences.l: And when he finished from his verse, he set-off hurrying until he came to the wolf, and said: God has made-easy for you the matters (on the way) to the vineyard without-toil.
sentences.i: When he had finished his verses he set off in haste and came to the wolf, and said, “God has smoothed your way to the vineyard, and with no toil at all.
sentences.n: sahhala, “to make easy”: God has cleared the way for you to the vineyard. The print runs bi-lā taʿabin together as بلاتعب; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: وَهَذَا مِنْ سَعَادَتِكَ فَهَنِيأً لَكَ بِمَافَتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ وَسَهَّلَ لَكَ مِنْ تِلْكَ الْغَنِيمَةِ السَّائِغَةِ وَالرِّزْقِ الْوَاسِعِ بِلَا مَشَقَّةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā min saʿādatika fa-hanīʾan laka bi-mā fataḥa allāhu ʿalayka wa-sahhala laka min tilka al-ghanīmati al-sāʾighati wa-al-rizqi al-wāsiʿi bi-lā mashaqqatin
sentences.l: And this (is) from your good-fortune; so may-it-do-good to you, with what God has opened upon you and made-easy for you of that spoil easy-to-swallow and the provision ample, without hardship.
sentences.i: This is your good luck: may you enjoy what God has opened to you and made easy for you, that plunder sweet to swallow and that ample provision, without any trouble.”
sentences.n: hanīʾan laka, “may it do you good, enjoy it”, a set wish, here spelt with the hamza on alif (usually هنيئا). fataḥa allāhu ʿalayhi, “God opened (a way of livelihood) to him”. sāʾigh, “easy to swallow, pleasant”. rizq, “provision, sustenance”, what God allots. The print runs bi-mā fataḥa together as بمافتح; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الذِّئْبُ لِلثَّعْلَبِ وَمَا الدَّلِيلُ عَلَى مَا وَصَفْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-dhiʾbu li-al-thaʿlabi wa-mā al-dalīlu ʿalā mā waṣafta
sentences.l: And the wolf said to the fox: And what (is) the proof of what you-described?
sentences.i: The wolf said to the fox, “And what proof have you of what you describe?”

sentences.t: قَالَ إِنِّي انْتَهَيْتُ إِلَى الْكَرْمِ فَوَجَدْتُ صَاحِبَهُ قَدْمَاتَ وَافْتَرَسَهُ الذِّئْبُ وَدَخَلْتُ الْبُسْتَانَ فَرَأَيْتُ الْأَثْمَارَ زَاهِيَةً عَلَى الْأَشْجَارِ
sentences.tr: qāla innī intahaytu ilā al-karmi fa-wajadtu ṣāḥibahu qad māta wa-iftarasahu al-dhiʾbu wa-dakhaltu al-bustāna fa-raʾaytu al-athmāra zāhiyatan ʿalā al-ashjāri
sentences.l: He said: I reached to the vineyard, and found its owner had died, and the wolf had-made-prey-of-him; and I entered the garden, and saw the fruits bright upon the trees.
sentences.i: He said, “I went as far as the vineyard and found that its owner was dead, killed and eaten by a wolf; and I went into the garden and saw the fruit glowing on the trees.”
sentences.n: A lie, of course: the fox has seen the covered pit. iftarasa, “to seize and devour (prey)”. al-dhiʾb, “the wolf”, here means a wolf, any wolf. The print runs qad māta together as قدمات; the spacing is kept. zāhiya, “bright, flourishing”. The shadda in انّي is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَشُكَّ الذِّئْبُ فِي قَوْلِ الثَّعْلَبِ وَأَدْرَكَهُ الشَّرَهُ فَقَامَ حَتَّى انْتَهَى إِلَى الثُّلْمَةِ وَقَدْ غَرَّهُ الطَّمَعُ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yashukka al-dhiʾbu fī qawli al-thaʿlabi wa-adrakahu al-sharahu fa-qāma ḥattā intahā ilā al-thulmati wa-qad gharrahu al-ṭamaʿu
sentences.l: And the wolf did-not doubt about the saying of the fox, and the gluttony overtook-him; so he rose until he reached to the breach, and the greed had deceived-him.
sentences.i: The wolf did not doubt the fox's word; gluttony seized him, and he got up and went to the breach in the wall, beguiled by greed.
sentences.n: sharah, “gluttony, greed”: its pointing is the print's own, as is the shadda in غرّه. thulma, “breach, gap” in a wall: the covered pit the fox found earlier lies in it. gharra, “to deceive, lure”.

sentences.t: وَوَقَفَ الثَّعْلَبُ مُتَهَافِتًا كَالْمَيِّتِ وَتَمَثَّلَ بِهَذَا الْبَيْتِ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-waqafa al-thaʿlabu mutahāfitan ka-al-mayyiti wa-tamaththala bi-hādhā al-bayti shiʿrun
sentences.l: And the fox stood collapsing like the dead, and quoted this verse — verse:
sentences.i: The fox stood there, limp as a dead thing, and quoted this line:
sentences.n: tahāfata, “to fall to pieces, collapse”, and also “to rush headlong (at something)”; mutahāfitan ka-al-mayyiti seems to picture the fox weak and swaying, whether with suppressed glee or in feigned exhaustion. tamaththala bi-, “to quote (a verse) as fitting”. shiʿr, “verse”, is the rubric that introduces the line.

sentences.t: اَتَطْمَعُ مِنْ لَيْلَى بِوَصْلٍ وَاِنَّمَا * تَضُرُّ بِاَعْنَاقِ الرِّجَالِ الْمَطَامِعُ
sentences.tr: a-taṭmaʿu min Laylā bi-waṣlin wa-innamā * taḍurru bi-aʿnāqi al-rijāli al-maṭāmiʿu
sentences.l: Do-you-covet from Laylā union? And only * do-harm to the necks of the men the cravings.
sentences.i: You hope for Laylā's favours? Yet it is cravings, * and nothing else, that bring men's necks to harm.
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own. Laylā is the stock beloved of Arabic love poetry; the fox quotes the line as a sly comment on the wolf's greed. waṣl, “union”, a lover's meeting. maṭāmiʿ (sing. maṭmaʿ), “objects of greed, cravings”: that greed cuts men's necks is proverbial. innamā, “only”, throws the weight onto the last word.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا انْتَهَى الذِّئْبُ إِلَى الثُّلْمَةِ قَالَ لَهُ الثَّعْلَبُ ادْخُلْ إِلَى الْكَرْمِ فَقَدْ كُفِيتَ مُؤْنَةَ التَّسْلِيقِ وَهَدْمِ حَائِطِ الْبُسْتَانِ وَعَلَى اللَّهِ تَمَامُ الْإِحْسَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā intahā al-dhiʾbu ilā al-thulmati qāla lahu al-thaʿlabu udkhul ilā al-karmi fa-qad kufīta muʾnata al-taslīqi wa-hadmi ḥāʾiṭi al-bustāni wa-ʿalā allāhi tamāmu al-iḥsāni
sentences.l: And when the wolf reached to the breach, the fox said to him: Enter into the vineyard, for you-have-been-spared the burden of the climbing and the demolishing of the wall of the garden; and upon God (is) the completion of the kindness.
sentences.i: When the wolf reached the breach, the fox said to him, “Go on into the vineyard: you have been spared the trouble of climbing the garden wall or breaking it down, and God will crown His kindness.”
sentences.n: kufiya muʾnata, “to be spared the trouble of”. taslīq is not a Classical form; it is evidently colloquial for “climbing” (Classical tasalluq), and is vocalised as printed. bustān/iḥsān rhyme. ʿalā allāhi tamāmu al-iḥsāni, “it is for God to complete the favour”, a pious formula, here a mockery.

sentences.t: فَأَقْبَلَ الذِّئْبُ مَاشِيًا يُرِيدُ الدُّخُولَ إِلَى الْكَرْمِ فَلَمَّا تَوَسَّطَ غِطَاءَ الثُّلْمَةِ هَوَى فِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-aqbala al-dhiʾbu māshiyan yurīdu al-dukhūla ilā al-karmi fa-lammā tawassaṭa ghiṭāʾa al-thulmati hawā fīhā
sentences.l: And the wolf came-forward walking, wanting the entering into the vineyard; and when he reached-the-middle-of the covering of the breach, he fell-down in-it.
sentences.i: The wolf came on at a walk, meaning to go into the vineyard, and when he was halfway across the covering of the breach he fell into the pit.
sentences.n: tawassaṭa, “to be in the middle of”. ghiṭāʾ, “cover, covering”: the thin lid laid over the pit. hawā, “to fall, drop down”.

sentences.t: فَاضْطَرَبَ الثَّعْلَبُ اضْطِرَابًا شَدِيدًا مِنَ السُّرُورِ وَالْفَرَحِ وَزَالَ عَنْهُ الْهَمُّ وَالتَّرَحُ وَأَطْرَبَ بِالنَّغَمَاتِ وَأَنْشَدَ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-iḍṭaraba al-thaʿlabu iḍṭirāban shadīdan mina al-surūri wa-al-faraḥi wa-zāla ʿanhu al-hammu wa-al-taraḥu wa-aṭraba bi-al-naghamāti wa-anshada hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And the fox shook a violent shaking from the joy and the gladness, and there-left from him the care and the sorrow; and he-made-merry with the tunes and recited these verses:
sentences.i: The fox quivered all over with joy and gladness; care and sorrow left him, and he struck up merry tunes and recited these lines:
sentences.n: iḍṭaraba, “to be agitated, quiver”, followed by its own verbal noun for emphasis. faraḥ and taraḥ, “joy” and “sorrow”, a rhyming pair. aṭraba is properly “to delight (someone)”; with bi-al-naghamāt, “with tunes”, it must mean he sang or trilled merrily.

sentences.t:
رَقَّ الزَّمَانُ لِحَالَتِيْ * وَرَثَى لِطُوْلِ تَحَرُّقِيْ
وَاَنَا لَنِيْ مَا اَشْتَهِيْ * وَاَزَالَ مِمَّا اَتَّقِيْ
فَلَاَ صْفَحَنْ عَمَّا جَنَا * هُ مِنَ الذُّنُوْبِ السُّبَّقِ
فَالذِّئْبُ لَيْسَ لَهُ خَلَا * صٌ مِنْ هَلَاكٍ مَوْبِقِ
وَالْكَرْمُ لِيْ وَحْدِيْ وَمَا * لِيْ مِنْ شَرِيْكٍ اَحْمَقِ
sentences.tr:
raqqa al-zamānu li-ḥālatī * wa-rathā li-ṭūli taḥarruqī
wa-anā lanī mā ashtahī * wa-azāla mimmā attaqī
fa-la-aṣfaḥan ʿammā janā * hu mina al-dhunūbi al-subbaqi
fa-al-dhiʾbu laysa lahu khalā * ṣun min halākin mawbiqi
wa-al-karmu lī waḥdī wa-mā * lī min sharīkin aḥmaqi
sentences.l:
Time grew-tender toward my state * and lamented for the length of my burning,
and granted-me what I-desire * and removed (some) of what I-fear.
So I-will-surely-pardon what it-committed * of the sins gone-before:
for the wolf, there-is-not for him an escape * from a ruin destroying,
and the vineyard (is) mine alone, and there-is-not * for-me any partner foolish.
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own. Two words are printed split: وَاَنَا لَنِيْ is wa-anālanī, “and it granted me”, and فَلَاَ صْفَحَنْ is fa-la-aṣfaḥan, “I shall surely pardon” (with the short energetic ending -an). Three lines carry a word across the half-line break (janā*hu, khalā*ṣun, wa-mā*lī), as the metre requires. Time (al-zamān) is the subject throughout: fortune has paid its debt to the fox. taḥarruq, “burning (with grief)”. subbaq, plural of sābiq, “former”; mawbiq, “destroying”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ نَظَرَ فِى الْحُفْرَةِ فَرَأَى الذِّئْبَ يَبْكِي نَدَمًا وَحُزْنًا عَلَى نَفْسِهِ فَبَكَى الثَّعْلَبُ مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu naẓara fī al-ḥufrati fa-raʾā al-dhiʾba yabkī nadaman wa-ḥuznan ʿalā nafsihi fa-bakā al-thaʿlabu maʿahu
sentences.l: Then he looked into the pit, and saw the wolf weeping (from) regret and grief over himself; and the fox wept with him.
sentences.i: Then he looked into the pit and saw the wolf weeping for remorse and grief at his own plight; and the fox wept with him.
sentences.n: thumma innahu, “then he …”, a common way of resuming the narrative. nadaman wa-ḥuznan, accusatives of cause: “out of regret and grief”.

sentences.t: فَرَفَعَ الذِّئْبُ رَأْسَهُ إِلَى الثَّعْلَبِ وَقَالَ لَهُ أَمِنْ رَحْمَتِكَ لِي بَكَيْتَ يَا أَبَا الْحُصَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-rafaʿa al-dhiʾbu raʾsahu ilā al-thaʿlabi wa-qāla lahu a-min raḥmatika lī bakayta yā Abā al-Ḥuṣayni
sentences.l: And the wolf raised his head to the fox, and said to him: Is-it-from your pity for-me (that) you-wept, O Abū al-Ḥuṣayn?
sentences.i: The wolf lifted his head to the fox and said, “Is it out of pity for me that you weep, O Abū al-Ḥuṣayn?”
sentences.n: Abū al-Ḥuṣayn, “father of the little fortress”, is the fox's kunya, the familiar name by which the fox is addressed in fable; ḥuṣayn is itself a name for the fox. a- asks the question; the fronted min raḥmatika puts the stress on the motive. The fatḥa on the opening alif of أمن is the print's own.

sentences.t: قَالَ لَا وَالَّذِي قَذَفَكَ فِي هَذِهِ الْحُفْرَةِ إِنَّمَا بَكَيْتُ لِطُولِ عُمْرِكَ الْمَاضِي وَأَسَفًا عَلَى كَوْنِكَ لَمْ تَقَعْ فِي هَذِهِ الثُّلْمَةِ قَبْلَ الْيَوْمِ
sentences.tr: qāla lā wa-alladhī qadhafaka fī hādhihi al-ḥufrati innamā bakaytu li-ṭūli ʿumrika al-māḍī wa-asafan ʿalā kawnika lam taqaʿ fī hādhihi al-thulmati qabla al-yawmi
sentences.l: He said: No, by-the-One-who flung-you into this pit! I-wept only for the length of your life (that is) past, and (in) regret over your being (that) you-did-not fall into this breach before today.
sentences.i: He said, “No, by Him who flung you into this pit! I wept only because your life has lasted so long, and for sorrow that you did not fall into this breach before today.
sentences.n: wa-alladhī …, “by Him who …”: an oath, with God named by what He has done; the fox's choice of deed is pure mockery. ʿalā kawnika lam taqaʿ, “over your having not fallen”: kawn, “being”, turns the clause into a noun.

sentences.t: وَلَوْ وَقَعْتَ فِيهَا قَبْلَ اجْتِمَاعِي بِكَ لَكُنْتُ أَرَحْتُ وَاسْتَرَحْتُ وَلَكِنْ أُبْقِيتَ إِلَى أَجَلِكَ الْمَحْتُومِ وَوَقْتِكَ الْمَعْلُومِ
sentences.tr: wa-law waqaʿta fīhā qabla ijtimāʿī bika la-kuntu araḥtu wa-istaraḥtu wa-lākin ubqīta ilā ajalika al-maḥtūmi wa-waqtika al-maʿlūmi
sentences.l: And if you-had-fallen into-it before my coming-together with-you, I-would-have given-rest and taken-rest; but you-were-kept-alive until your term decreed and your time known.
sentences.i: Had you fallen into it before I ever fell in with you, I should have had peace and rest; but you were spared until your fated end and your appointed hour.”
sentences.n: araḥtu wa-istaraḥtu, “I would have given rest and found rest”, a jingle: everyone would have been the better for it. ubqīta, passive, “you were left (alive)”. ajal, “appointed term (of life)”; maḥtūm/maʿlūm rhyme.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الذِّئْبُ كَالْمَازِحِ أَيُّهَا الْمُسِيءُ فِي فِعْلِهِ رُحْ لِوَالِدَتِي وَأَخْبِرْهَا بِمَا حَصَلَ لِي لَعَلَّهَا تَحْتَالُ عَلَى خَلَاصِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-dhiʾbu ka-al-māziḥi ayyuhā al-musīʾu fī fiʿlihi ruḥ li-wālidatī wa-akhbirhā bi-mā ḥaṣala lī laʿallahā taḥtālu ʿalā khalāṣī
sentences.l: And the wolf said to him, as-one-jesting: O the-wrongdoer in his deed, go to my mother and inform-her of what happened to-me; perhaps she will-contrive for my deliverance.
sentences.i: The wolf said to him, as if in jest, “You villain, go to my mother and tell her what has befallen me; perhaps she can find some way to get me out.”
sentences.n: ka-al-māziḥ, “like one joking”: the wolf tries to make light of it. ruḥ, “go!”, from rāḥa, is the everyday imperative, Middle Arabic in flavour. iḥtāla ʿalā, “to find a stratagem for”. The shadda in لعلّها is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الثَّعْلَبُ لَقَدْ أَوْقَعَكَ فِى الْهَلَاكِ شِدَّةُ طَمَعِكَ وَكَثْرَةُ حِرْصِكَ حَيْثُ سَقَطْتَ فِي حُفْرَةٍ لَسْتَ مِنْهَا بِسَالِمٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-thaʿlabu la-qad awqaʿaka fī al-halāki shiddatu ṭamaʿika wa-kathratu ḥirṣika ḥaythu saqaṭta fī ḥufratin lasta minhā bi-sālimin
sentences.l: And the fox said to him: Indeed there-has-cast-you into the ruin the intensity of your greed and the abundance of your covetousness, since you-fell into a pit (that) you-are-not from-it safe.
sentences.i: The fox said to him, “It was the violence of your greed and the excess of your craving that cast you into ruin, now that you have fallen into a pit you will not come out of safe.
sentences.n: The verb awqaʿa comes first, in the masculine, before its feminine subject shidda: normal when other words intervene. ḥirṣ, “avidity, covetousness”. lasta … bi-sālimin: bi- marks the predicate of laysa.

sentences.t: أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الذِّئْبُ الْجَاهِلُ أَنَّ صَاحِبَ الْمَثَلِ السَّائِرِ يَقُولُ مَنْ لَمْ يُفَكِّرْ فِى الْعَوَاقِبِ مَا الدَّهْرُ لَهُ بِصَاحِبٍ وَلَمْ يَأْمَنِ الْمَعَاطِبَ
sentences.tr: a-lam taʿlam ayyuhā al-dhiʾbu al-jāhilu anna ṣāḥiba al-mathali al-sāʾiri yaqūlu man lam yufakkir fī al-ʿawāqibi mā al-dahru lahu bi-ṣāḥibin wa-lam yaʾmani al-maʿāṭiba
sentences.l: Did-you-not know, O wolf the ignorant, that the owner of the proverb current says: Whoever does-not think about the consequences, not (is) the Time to-him a companion, and he-is-not safe-from the perils?
sentences.i: Do you not know, you ignorant wolf, what the author of the well-worn proverb says: ‘Whoever does not think of consequences, Time is no friend to him, and he is never safe from perils’?”
sentences.n: mathal sāʾir, “a current proverb”, one that “travels” from mouth to mouth. The saying rhymes in -āqib/-āḥib/-āṭib. mā … bi-ṣāḥibin: mā negates like laysa, with bi- before the predicate. al-dahr, “Time, fortune”, the force that turns on men. maʿāṭib (sing. maʿṭab), “places or causes of ruin”. The hamza in يأمن is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الذِّئْبُ لِلثَّعْلَبِ يَا أَبَا الْحُصَيْنِ إِنَّمَا كُنْتَ تُظْهِرُ مَحَبَّتِي وَتَرْغَبُ فِي مَوَدَّتِي وَتَخَافُ مِنْ شِدَّةِ قُوَّتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-dhiʾbu li-al-thaʿlabi yā Abā al-Ḥuṣayni innamā kunta tuẓhiru maḥabbatī wa-targhabu fī mawaddatī wa-takhāfu min shiddati quwwatī
sentences.l: And the wolf said to the fox: O Abū al-Ḥuṣayn, you used-to only show love-of-me and desire my friendship and fear the intensity of my strength.
sentences.i: The wolf said to the fox, “O Abū al-Ḥuṣayn, you always made a show of loving me; you sought my friendship and feared my great strength.
sentences.n: maḥabbatī, “my love”, here love for me. maḥabbatī/mawaddatī/quwwatī rhyme. The wolf is reminding the fox of the footing they used to be on.

sentences.t: فَلَا تَحْقِدْ عَلَيَّ بِمَا فَعَلْتُ مَعَكَ فَمَنْ قَدَرَ وَعَفَا كَانَ أَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَقَدْ قَالَ الشَّاعِرُ
sentences.tr: fa-lā taḥqid ʿalayya bi-mā faʿaltu maʿaka fa-man qadara wa-ʿafā kāna ajruhu ʿalā allāhi wa-qad qāla al-shāʿiru
sentences.l: So do-not bear-a-grudge against-me for what I-did with-you; for whoever had-power and pardoned, his reward was upon God. And the poet has said:
sentences.i: So bear me no grudge for what I did to you: whoever has the power and forgives, his reward is with God. And the poet has said:
sentences.n: ḥaqada ʿalā, “to bear a grudge against”. faʿala maʿa, “to do with”, is the everyday idiom for “to treat (someone)”. fa-man … ʿafā … ajruhu ʿalā allāhi echoes the Qurʾān (42:40), “whoever pardons and makes peace, his reward is with God”. The shadda in عليّ is the print's own.

sentences.t:
اِزْرَعْ جَمِيلًا وَلَوْ فِي غَيْرِ مَوْضِعِهِ * مَا خَابَ قَطُّ جَمِيلٌ اَيْنَمَا زُرِعَا
اِنَّ الْجَمِيلَ وَاِنْ طَالَ الزَّمَانُ بِهِ * فَلَيْسَ يَحْصُدُهُ اِلَّا الَّذِي زَرَعَا
sentences.tr:
izraʿ jamīlan wa-law fī ghayri mawḍiʿihi * mā khāba qaṭṭu jamīlun aynamā zuriʿā
inna al-jamīla wa-in ṭāla al-zamānu bihi * fa-laysa yaḥṣuduhu illā alladhī zaraʿā
sentences.l:
Sow a-kindness, even-if in other-than its place; * never failed at-all a kindness wherever it-was-sown.
Indeed the kindness, even-if the time grows-long with it, * there-is-not reaping-it except the-one-who sowed.
sentences.i:
Sow kindness, though it fall on unfit ground; * no kindness ever failed, wherever it was sown.
A kindness, however long it waits, * is reaped by none but him who sowed it.”
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own. Well-known lines on doing good. The final -ā of zuriʿā and zaraʿā is the long vowel of the rhyme, not a dual. qaṭṭu, “ever”, goes with a negated past, as here.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الثَّعْلَبُ يَا أَجْهَلَ السِّبَاعِ وَأَحْمَقَ الْوُحُوشِ فِى الْبِقَاعِ هَلْ نَسِيتَ تَجَبُّرَكَ وَعُتُوَّكَ وَتَكَبُّرَكَ وَأَنْتَ لَمْ تَرْعَ حَقَّ الْمُعَاشَرَةِ وَ لَمْ تَنْتَصِحْ بِقَوْلِ الشَّاعِرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-thaʿlabu yā ajhala al-sibāʿi wa-aḥmaqa al-wuḥūshi fī al-biqāʿi hal nasīta tajabburaka wa-ʿutuwwaka wa-takabburaka wa-anta lam tarʿa ḥaqqa al-muʿāsharati wa-lam tantaṣiḥ bi-qawli al-shāʿiri
sentences.l: And the fox said to him: O most-ignorant of the beasts-of-prey and most-foolish of the wild-beasts in the lands! Have-you forgotten your tyranny and your insolence and your arrogance, while you did-not observe the due of the living-together, and did-not take-advice from the saying of the poet:
sentences.i: The fox said to him, “O most ignorant of beasts of prey, most foolish of the wild beasts of the earth! Have you forgotten your tyranny, your insolence and your pride, when you paid no regard to what you owed a companion, and took no advice from the poet's words:
sentences.n: sibāʿ (sing. sabuʿ), “beasts of prey”; biqāʿ (sing. buqʿa), “tracts of land”: the two rhyme. raʿā ḥaqqa, “to respect the right of”; muʿāshara, “living together, companionship”. intaṣaḥa bi-, “to take advice from”. The print sets wa- at the end of one line and lam at the start of the next; the spacing is kept. The shaddas in تجبّرك and عتوّك are the print's own.

sentences.t:
لَا تَظْلِمَنَّ اِذَا مَا كُنْتَ مُقْتَدِرًا * اِنَّ الظَّلُومَ عَلَى حَدٍّ مِنَ النَّقَمِ
تَنَامُ عَيْنَيْكَ وَالْمَظْلُومُ مُنْتَبِهٌ * يَدْعُو عَلَيْكَ وَعَيْنُ اللّٰهِ لَمْ تَنَمِ
sentences.tr:
lā taẓlimanna idhā mā kunta muqtadiran * inna al-ẓalūma ʿalā ḥaddin mina al-naqami
tanāmu ʿaynayka wa-al-maẓlūmu muntabihun * yadʿū ʿalayka wa-ʿaynu allāhi lam tanami
sentences.l:
Do-not do-wrong when you-are able; * indeed the wrongdoer (is) on an edge of the vengeances.
Your two-eyes sleep while the wronged (is) awake, * praying against you, and the eye of God did-not sleep.
sentences.i:
Do no wrong when you have the power: * the oppressor stands on the brink of vengeance.
Your eyes sleep; the one you wronged lies awake * and calls down curses on you, and the eye of God never sleeps.”
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own. Much-quoted lines against oppression. lā taẓlimanna: a prohibition strengthened by the energetic -anna. ʿaynayka is the dual in its oblique form where Classical grammar wants the subject form ʿaynāka; the print points it so. naqam (sing. niqma), “vengeance, punishment”. daʿā ʿalā, “to pray against, curse”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الذِّئْبُ يَا أَبَا الْحُصَيْنِ لَاتُؤَاخِذْنِي بِسَابِقِ الذُّنُوبِ فَالْعَفْوُ مِنَ الْكِرَامِ مَطْلُوبٌ وَصُنْعُ الْمَعْرُوفِ مِنْ أَحْسَنِ الذَّخَائِرِ وَمَا أَحْسَنَ قَوْلَ الشَّاعِرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-dhiʾbu yā Abā al-Ḥuṣayni lā tuʾākhidhnī bi-sābiqi al-dhunūbi fa-al-ʿafwu mina al-kirāmi maṭlūbun wa-ṣunʿu al-maʿrūfi min aḥsani al-dhakhāʾiri wa-mā aḥsana qawla al-shāʿiri
sentences.l: And the wolf said to him: O Abū al-Ḥuṣayn, do-not take-me-to-task for the former of the sins; for the pardon from the noble-ones (is) sought, and the doing of the kindness (is) of the best of the treasures-laid-up. And how fine (is) the saying of the poet:
sentences.i: The wolf said to him, “O Abū al-Ḥuṣayn, do not hold my past sins against me: pardon is what one looks for from the noble, and a kindness done is among the best of treasures laid up. How well the poet puts it:
sentences.n: ākhadha bi-, “to hold (someone) to account for”. al-dhunūb/maṭlūb rhyme. dhakhāʾir (sing. dhakhīra), “stores laid up for later”. mā aḥsana …, “how fine is …!”, the verb of wonder, with its object in the accusative. The print runs lā tuʾākhidhnī together as لاتؤاخذني; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: بَادِرْ بِخَيْرٍ اِذَا مَا كُنْتَ مُقْتَدِرًا * فَلَيْسَ فِي كُلِّ حِينٍ أَنْتَ مُقْتَدِرًا
sentences.tr: bādir bi-khayrin idhā mā kunta muqtadiran * fa-laysa fī kulli ḥīnin anta muqtadirā
sentences.l: Hasten with good when you-are able; * for not in every time (are) you able.
sentences.i: Be quick to do good while you have the power; * you will not have the power at every hour.”
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own. bādara bi-, “to hasten to do”. laysa takes anta as its subject and muqtadiran as its predicate; at the rhyme it is read muqtadirā. Both half-lines end on the same word, a stock device.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلِ الذِّئْبُ يَتَذَلَّلُ لِلثَّعْلَبِ وَيَقُولُ لَهُ لَعَلَّكَ تَقْدِرُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ تُخَلِّصُنِي بِهِ مِنَ الْهَلَاكِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazali al-dhiʾbu yatadhallalu li-al-thaʿlabi wa-yaqūlu lahu laʿallaka taqdiru ʿalā shayʾin tukhalliṣunī bihi mina al-halāki
sentences.l: And the wolf did-not cease humbling-himself to the fox and saying to him: Perhaps you are-able-for a thing (by which) you-will-free-me with-it from the perishing.
sentences.i: And the wolf kept abasing himself before the fox, saying, “Perhaps you can find some way to save me from destruction.”
sentences.n: lam yazal, “he did not cease”: with a following imperfect, “he kept on doing”. tadhallala li-, “to humble oneself before”. tukhalliṣunī bihi describes shayʾ, “a thing by which you may free me”: an indefinite noun takes its descriptive clause without alladhī, and bihi points back to it.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الثَّعْلَبُ أَيُّهَا الذِّئْبُ الْجَاهِلُ الْمَغْرُورُ الْمَاكِرُ الْغَادِرُ لَاتَطْمَعْ فِى الْخَلَاصِ فَإِنَّ هَذَا جَزَاءٌ لِقَبِيحِ فِعْلِكَ وَقِصَاصٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-thaʿlabu ayyuhā al-dhiʾbu al-jāhilu al-maghrūru al-mākiru al-ghādiru lā taṭmaʿ fī al-khalāṣi fa-inna hādhā jazāʾun li-qabīḥi fiʿlika wa-qiṣāṣun
sentences.l: And the fox said to him: O you the wolf, the ignorant, the deluded, the cunning, the treacherous! Do-not covet (hope) in the deliverance; for this (is) a recompense for the foulness-of your deed, and a retaliation.
sentences.i: The fox said to him, “O ignorant, deluded, cunning, treacherous wolf, do not hope for deliverance: this is the reward of your foul doings, and their just retribution.”
sentences.n: ṭamiʿa fī, “to hope for, covet”. qiṣāṣ is retaliation in kind, the law of like for like. The adjectives fall in pairs, al-jāhil al-maghrūr and al-mākir al-ghādir. The print runs lā taṭmaʿ together as لاتطمع; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ ضَحِكَ بِالشِّدْقَيْنِ وَأَنْشَدَ هَذَيْنِ الْبَيْتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: thumma ḍaḥika bi-al-shidqayni wa-anshada hādhayni al-baytayni
sentences.l: Then he laughed with the two-corners-of-the-mouth, and recited these two verses:
sentences.i: Then he laughed from ear to ear and recited these two lines:
sentences.n: shidq, “the corner of the mouth”; to laugh bi-al-shidqayn, “with both corners”, is to laugh openly, with the whole mouth.

sentences.t:
لَا تُكْثِرَنَّ خِدَاعِيْ * فَلَنْ تَنَالَ مَنَالًا
مَا رُمْتَ مِنِّيْ مُحَالُ * زَرَعْتَ فَاحْصُدْ وَبَالًا
sentences.tr:
lā tukthiranna khidāʿī * fa-lan tanāla manālan
mā rumta minnī muḥālun * zaraʿta fa-uḥṣud wabālan
sentences.l:
Do-not multiply deceiving-me, * for you-will-never attain an-attainment;
what you-sought from-me (is) impossible: * you-sowed, so reap ruin.
sentences.i:
Do not ply me with tricks: * you will gain nothing by it.
What you want of me cannot be: * you sowed, now reap the harvest of ruin.
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own. tukthiranna, prohibition strengthened with the energetic -anna. tanāla manālan, “attain an attainment”: the verb with its own noun for emphasis. rāma, “to seek, desire”; wabāl, “ill consequence, ruin”. The print ends muḥālu with a single ḍamma for muḥālun.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الذِّئْبُ يَا حَلِيمَ السِّبَاعِ أَنْتَ عِنْدِي أَوْثَقُ مِنْ أَنْ تُسْلِمَنِي فِي هَذِهِ الْحُفْرَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-dhiʾbu yā ḥalīma al-sibāʿi anta ʿindī awthaqu min an tuslimanī fī hādhihi al-ḥufrati
sentences.l: And the wolf said to him: O forbearing-one of the beasts-of-prey, you (are) with-me more-trustworthy than that you-should-abandon-me in this pit.
sentences.i: The wolf said to him, “O most forbearing of beasts, I trust you too well to think you would leave me to my fate in this pit.”
sentences.n: ḥalīm, “forbearing, mild, slow to anger”, a flattering title. sibāʿ, “beasts of prey”. awthaqu min an, “more trustworthy than that”: too trustworthy to. aslama, “to give up, abandon (someone to his fate)”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَكَى وَاشْتَكَى وَأَفَاضَ دَمْعَ الْعَيْنَيْنِ وَأَنْشَدَ هَذَيْنِ الْبَيْتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: thumma bakā wa-ishtakā wa-afāḍa damʿa al-ʿaynayni wa-anshada hādhayni al-baytayni
sentences.l: Then he wept and complained, and poured-out the tears of the two-eyes, and recited these two verses:
sentences.i: Then he wept and lamented, his eyes streaming with tears, and recited these two lines:
sentences.n: bakā and ishtakā rhyme. afāḍa, “to make overflow, pour out”.

sentences.t:
يَامَنْ اَيَادِيْهِ عِنْدِى غَيْرُ وَاحِدَةٍ * وَمَنْ مَوَاهِبُهُ تَنْمُوْ عَنِ الْعَدَدِ
مَا نَابَنِيْ مِنْ زَمَانِيْ قَطُّ نَائِبَةٌ * اِلَّا وَجَدْتُكُ فِيْهَا آخِذًا بِيَدِيْ
sentences.tr:
yā man ayādīhi ʿindī ghayru wāḥidatin * wa-man mawāhibuhu tanmū ʿani al-ʿadadi
mā nābanī min zamānī qaṭṭu nāʾibatun * illā wajadtuku fīhā ākhidhan bi-yadī
sentences.l:
O whose hands (favours) with-me (are) not one, * and whose gifts grow beyond the counting!
There befell-me not from my time ever a calamity * but I-found-you in-it taking my hand.
sentences.i:
O you whose kindnesses to me are more than one, * whose gifts have grown past counting:
never did fortune bring me a single blow * but I found you there, holding me by the hand.
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own, and the print sets yā man as one word, يامن. ayādī, plural of yad, “hand”, here “favours, benefactions”, an old sense of the word. ghayru wāḥidatin, “not one”: many. nāba, “to befall”, and nāʾiba, “a misfortune”, are from the same root. The print points wajadtuku with a ḍamma on the kāf, where the sense needs wajadtuka, “I found you”; the mark is kept as printed. ākhidhan bi-yadī, “taking my hand”: helping me up. Conventional lines of praise to a patron, put in the wolf's mouth as flattery.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الثَّعْلَبُ أَيُّهَا الْعَدُوُّ الْأَحْمَقُ كَيْفَ صِرْتَ إِلَى التَّضَرُّعِ وَالْخُشُوعِ وَالذِّلَّةِ وَالْخُضُوعِ بَعْدَ الْأَنَفَةِ وَالتَّكَبُّرِ وَالظُّلْمِ وَالتَّجَبُّرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-thaʿlabu ayyuhā al-ʿaduwwu al-aḥmaqu kayfa ṣirta ilā al-taḍarruʿi wa-al-khushūʿi wa-al-dhillati wa-al-khuḍūʿi baʿda al-anafati wa-al-takabburi wa-al-ẓulmi wa-al-tajabburi
sentences.l: And the fox said to him: O you the enemy, the fool! How have-you-come to the beseeching and the humbleness, and the abjectness and the submission, after the disdain and the arrogance, and the oppression and the tyranny?
sentences.i: The fox said to him, “You foolish enemy! How have you come down to pleading and meekness, abasement and submission, after all your pride and arrogance, your oppression and tyranny?
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-khushūʿ / al-khuḍūʿ, then al-takabbur / al-tajabbur. ṣāra ilā, “to come to, end up in”. anafa, “haughtiness, disdain”.

sentences.t: لَقَدْ صَحِبْتُكَ خَائِفًا مِنْ عُدْوَانِكَ وَتَمَلَّقْتُ لَكَ لَارَغْبَةً فِي إِحْسَانِكَ
sentences.tr: la-qad ṣaḥibtuka khāʾifan min ʿudwānika wa-tamallaqtu laka lā raghbatan fī iḥsānika
sentences.l: Indeed I-kept-company-with-you fearing your aggression, and I-flattered you, not (out of) desire for your kindness.
sentences.i: I kept company with you only for fear of your violence, and I flattered you, not because I hoped for any kindness from you.
sentences.n: ʿudwān and iḥsān close the two rhyming members. tamallaqa li-, “to fawn on, flatter”. lā raghbatan, “not out of desire”, the accusative of motive under negation. The print runs lā raghbatan together as لارغبة; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: وَالْآنَ نَزَلَتْ بِكَ الرَّجْفَةُ وَحَلَّتْ بِكَ النِّقْمَةُ وَأَنْشَدَ هَذَيْنِ الْبَيْتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-āna nazalat bika al-rajfatu wa-ḥallat bika al-niqmatu wa-anshada hādhayni al-baytayni
sentences.l: And now the quaking has-come-down on you, and the vengeance has-alighted on you.” And he recited these two verses:
sentences.i: And now the earthquake has come down upon you, and vengeance has fallen on you.” And he recited these two lines:
sentences.n: al-rajfa, “the quaking, the earthquake”, is a Qurʾānic word for the punishment that overtakes the wicked. nazala bi- and ḥalla bi-, “to come down upon, befall”: bi- marks the victim. al-rajfa / al-niqma rhyme.

sentences.t:
يَا اَيُّهَا الْمُلْتَمِسُ الْخَدِيْعَة * وَقَعْتَ فيْ نِيَّتِكَ الشَّنِيْعَةْ
فَذُقْ وَبَالَ الْمِحْنَةِ الْفَظِيْعَةْ * وَكُنْ مَعَ الذِّيَابِ فِيْ قَطِيْعَةْ
sentences.tr:
yā ayyuhā al-multamisu al-khadīʿah * waqaʿta fī niyyatika al-shanīʿah
fa-dhuq wabāla al-miḥnati al-faẓīʿah * wa-kun maʿa al-dhiyābi fī qaṭīʿah
sentences.l:
O you the seeker of the deceit, * you-have-fallen into your intent, the foul;
so taste the ill-consequence of the trial, the dreadful, * and be with the wolves in severance.
sentences.i:
O you who went seeking to deceive, * you have fallen into your own foul design;
so taste the bitter fruit of this dreadful trial, * and be cut off from the wolves, your kin.
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own, and the rhyme-words are pointed for the pause, -ah. The metre is rajaz, with all four half-lines rhyming. waqaʿta fī niyyatika, “you fell into your own intent”: the pit you dug is your own scheme. al-dhiyāb is al-dhiʾāb, “the wolves”, with the hamza softened. qaṭīʿa, “estrangement, severance”: the line is most likely “be at a break with the wolves”, cut off from your own kind.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الذِّئْبُ أَيُّهَا الْحَلِيمُ لَاتَكُنْ بِلِسَانِ أَهْلِ الْعَدَاوَةِ نَاطِقًا وَبِعَيْنِهِمْ مُحَدِّقًا وَكُنْ وَافِيًا بِعَهْدِ ائْتِلَافِي قَبْلَ أَنْ يَفُوتَ وَقْتُ التَّلَافِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-dhiʾbu ayyuhā al-ḥalīmu lā takun bi-lisāni ahli al-ʿadāwati nāṭiqan wa-bi-ʿaynihim muḥaddiqan wa-kun wāfiyan bi-ʿahdi iʾtilāfī qabla an yafūta waqtu al-talāfī
sentences.l: And the wolf said to him: O you the forbearing, do-not be with the tongue of the people of the enmity speaking, and with their eye staring; and be faithful to the covenant of my fellowship, before the time of the remedying passes.
sentences.i: The wolf said to him, “O forbearing one, do not speak with the tongue of enemies, nor look at me with their eyes; keep faith with the bond of our friendship, before the time for setting things right is gone.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose in pairs: nāṭiqan / muḥaddiqan, iʾtilāfī / al-talāfī, the last a play on two words of near-identical sound. ḥaddaqa, “to stare, fix the eyes”. wafā bi-, “to keep (a promise)”. talāfī, “making good, remedying (before it is too late)”. The print runs lā takun together as لاتكن; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: وَقُمْ وَتَسَبَّبْ لِي فِي حَبْلٍ تَشُدُّ طَرَفَهُ فِي شَجَرَةٍ وَتُدْلِي طَرَفَهُ الْآخَرَ إِلَيَّ حَتَّى أَتَعَلَّقَ بِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qum wa-tasabbab lī fī ḥablin tashuddu ṭarafahu fī shajaratin wa-tudlī ṭarafahu al-ākhara ilayya ḥattā ataʿallaqa bihi
sentences.l: And rise, and contrive for me (by way of) a rope: you-tie its end to a tree and you-let-down its other end to me, so-that I-may-cling to-it.
sentences.i: Get up and find me a rope: tie one end to a tree and let the other end down to me, so that I can catch hold of it.
sentences.n: tasabbaba fī, “to find the means for, see to”. The print writes the shadda on تشدّ, اليّ and اتعلّق; the rest is ours. adlā, “to let down (a rope or bucket)”: tudlī. ḥattā with the subjunctive, “so that”.

sentences.t: لَعَلِّي أَنْجُو مِمَّا أَنَا فِيهِ وَأَدْفَعُ لَكَ جَمِيعَ مَاحَوَتْهُ يَدِي مِنَ الذَّخَائِرِ
sentences.tr: laʿallī anjū mimmā anā fīhi wa-adfaʿu laka jamīʿa mā ḥawathu yadī mina al-dhakhāʾiri
sentences.l: Perhaps-I will-escape from-what I (am) in-it; and I-will-hand to you all-of what my hand has-gathered of the treasures.
sentences.i: Perhaps I may escape from this plight; and I will give you all the treasures my hand has gathered.”
sentences.n: laʿallī, “perhaps I”: the shadda is the print's. ḥawā, “to gather, contain”: mā ḥawathu yadī, “what my hand holds”, yad being feminine. dhakhāʾir, “stores, treasures laid by”. The print runs mā ḥawathu together as ماحوته; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الثَّعْلَبُ لَقَدْ أَكْثَرْتَ مِنَ الْمُحَاوَرَةِ فِيمَا لَيْسَ فِيهِ خَلَاصُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-thaʿlabu la-qad aktharta mina al-muḥāwarati fīmā laysa fīhi khalāṣuka
sentences.l: And the fox said to him: Indeed you-have-made-much of the parleying about what is-not in-it your deliverance.
sentences.i: The fox said to him, “You have talked a great deal about something that holds no deliverance for you.
sentences.n: akthara min, “to do much of”. muḥāwara, “exchange of words, debate”. The hamza on أكثرت is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَلَا تَطْمَعْ فِي ذَلِكَ فَلَنْ تَنَالَ مِنِّي مَا تُمْسِكُ بِهِ نَفْسَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lā taṭmaʿ fī dhālika fa-lan tanāla minnī mā tumsiku bihi nafsaka
sentences.l: So do-not covet that; for you-will-never obtain from-me what you-may-hold with-it your-self (alive).
sentences.i: So do not set your hopes on it: you will get nothing from me to keep yourself alive.
sentences.n: mā tumsiku bihi nafsaka is read “that by which you might hold on to your life”: amsaka nafsahu, “to keep oneself (alive), hold oneself back from ruin”. It could also be pointed tamassaku bihi nafsuka, “what your soul clings to”, with the same sense: the hope you are clutching at.

sentences.t: وَاذْكُرْ مَا سَلَفَ مِنْ سُوءِ فِعْلِكَ وَمَا تُضْمِرُهُ لِي مِنَ الْغَدْرِ وَالْمَكْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-udhkur mā salafa min sūʾi fiʿlika wa-mā tuḍmiruhu lī mina al-ghadri wa-al-makri
sentences.l: And remember what has-gone-before of the evil of your deed, and what you-conceal for me of the treachery and the cunning.
sentences.i: Remember your past misdeeds, and the treachery and cunning you harbour against me.
sentences.n: salafa, “to go before, be past”. aḍmara, “to conceal (in the heart), harbour”.

sentences.t: وَأَيْنَ أَنْتَ مِنَ الرَّجْمِ بِالْحِجَارَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-ayna anta mina al-rajmi bi-al-ḥijārati
sentences.l: And where (are) you from the pelting with the stones?
sentences.i: And how will you get away from the stones that will be hurled at you?
sentences.n: ayna anta min …, literally “where are you from …?”, often means “how far you are from …”. Here the fox seems to mean the opposite of comfort: “and what of the stoning?”, how will you escape it, when men find you in the pit. rajm, “stoning, pelting”.

sentences.t: وَاعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ ذَاتَكَ لِلدُّنْيَا مُفَارِقَةٌ وَمِنْهَا زَائِلَةٌ وَعَنْهَا رَاحِلَةٌ ثُمَّ تَصِيرُ إِلَى الدَّمَارِ وَسُوءِ الدَّارِ فَبِئْسَ الْقَرَارُ
sentences.tr: wa-iʿlam bi-anna dhātaka li-al-dunyā mufāriqatun wa-minhā zāʾilatun wa-ʿanhā rāḥilatun thumma taṣīru ilā al-damāri wa-sūʾi al-dāri fa-biʾsa al-qarāru
sentences.l: And know that your self (is) to the world parting, and from-it vanishing, and from-it departing; then it-will-come to the destruction and the evil of the abode — and wretched (is) the resting-place!
sentences.i: Know that your life is leaving this world, passing out of it, departing from it, and will come at last to ruin and an evil home: and wretched is that resting place!”
sentences.n: The print has ذانك, a misprint for ذاتك, corrected here: the feminine adjectives mufāriqa, zāʾila, rāḥila need the feminine dhāt, “self”. iʿlam bi-anna, “know that”, with an extra bi-. al-damār / al-dār / al-qarār rhyme. biʾsa al-qarār echoes the Qurʾān's phrase for Hell, “an evil place to settle”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الذِّئْبُ يَا أَبَا الْحُصَيْنِ كُنْ قَرِيبَ الرُّجُوعِ إِلَي الْوِدَادِ وَلَا تُصِرَّ عَلَى ضَغَائِنِ الْأَحْقَادِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-dhiʾbu yā Abā al-Ḥuṣayni kun qarība al-rujūʿi ilā al-widādi wa-lā tuṣirra ʿalā ḍaghāʾini al-aḥqādi
sentences.l: And the wolf said to him: O Abū al-Ḥuṣayn, be near-of the returning to the affection, and do-not persist in the grudges of the hatreds.
sentences.i: The wolf said to him, “O Abū al-Ḥuṣayn, be quick to return to friendship, and do not cling to old grudges and spite.
sentences.n: qarīb al-rujūʿ, “near of returning”: quick to come back. aṣarra ʿalā, “to persist in”. ilā is written here with a dotted yāʾ, الي. al-widād / al-aḥqād rhyme; ḍaghāʾin and aḥqād are near-synonyms, “rancours” and “hatreds”.

sentences.t: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ مَنْ خَلَّصَ نَفْسًا مِنَ الْهَلَاكِ فَقَدْ أَحْيَاهَا وَمَنْ أَحْيَاهَا فَكَأَنَّمَا أَحْيَى النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا
sentences.tr: wa-iʿlam anna man khallaṣa nafsan mina al-halāki fa-qad aḥyāhā wa-man aḥyāhā fa-ka-annamā aḥyā al-nāsa jamīʿan
sentences.l: And know that whoever frees a soul from the perishing has given-it-life; and whoever gives-it-life, it-is-as-though he-gave-life-to the people all-together.
sentences.i: And know that whoever saves a soul from destruction has given it life; and whoever gives it life, it is as though he had given life to all mankind.
sentences.n: The last clause is from the Qurʾān (5:32), “and whoever saves a life, it is as though he had saved the life of all mankind”. aḥyā is spelt احيى here, with a final yāʾ, and احياها with alif before the suffix.

sentences.t: وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ الْفَسَادَ فَإِنَّ الْحُكَمَاءَ نَهَوْا عَنْهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lā tattabiʿi al-fasāda fa-inna al-ḥukamāʾa nahaw ʿanhu
sentences.l: And do-not follow the corruption, for the wise-ones have-forbidden it.
sentences.i: Do not follow the way of wickedness, for the wise have forbidden it;
sentences.n: nahā ʿan, “to forbid”. fasād, “wrongdoing, mischief”: the word the fox once used of the wolf, now turned back on him.

sentences.t: وَلَافَسَادَ أَظْهَرُ مِنْ كَوْنِي فِي تِلْكَ الْحُفْرَةِ أَتَجَرَّعُ غُصَصَ الْمَوْتِ وَأَنْظُرُ إِلَى الْهَلَاكِ وَأَنْتَ قَادِرٌ عَلَى خَلَاصِي مِنَ الِارْتِبَاكِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā fasāda aẓharu min kawnī fī tilka al-ḥufrati atajarraʿu ghuṣaṣa al-mawti wa-anẓuru ilā al-halāki wa-anta qādirun ʿalā khalāṣī mina al-irtibāki
sentences.l: And no corruption (is) more-manifest than my being in that pit, gulping the chokings of the death and looking at the perishing, while you (are) able for my deliverance from the entanglement.
sentences.i: and there is no wickedness plainer than this: that I lie in that pit swallowing the bitter draughts of death and staring destruction in the face, while you are able to free me from my plight.
sentences.n: The print has ولانساد, a misprint for ولافساد, corrected here; it keeps lā fasāda run together as one word. lā fasāda, “there is no wickedness”: lā of absolute denial with the noun in the accusative. tajarraʿa, “to gulp down”; ghuṣaṣ, “chokings, lumps in the throat”: ghuṣaṣ al-mawt are the throes of death. al-halāk / al-irtibāk rhyme; irtibāk, “entanglement, being caught fast”.

sentences.t: فَجُدْ عَلَيَّ بِالْخَلَاصِ وَافْعَلْ مَعِي جَمِيلًا
sentences.tr: fa-jud ʿalayya bi-al-khalāṣi wa-ifʿal maʿī jamīlan
sentences.l: So be-generous to-me with the deliverance, and do with-me a kindness.
sentences.i: So be generous and set me free, and do me a kindness.”
sentences.n: jāda ʿalā … bi-, “to bestow (something) generously on (someone)”: bi- marks the gift. jamīl, “a fine deed, a kindness”. The shadda on عليّ is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الثَّعْلَبُ أَيُّهَا الْفَظُّ الْغَلِيظُ إِنِّي أُشَبِّهُكَ فِي حُسْنِ عَلَانِيَتِكَ وَقَوْلِكَ وَأَقِيسُ قُبْحَ نِيَّتِكَ وَفِعْلِكَ بِالْبَازِي مَعَ الْحَجَلِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-thaʿlabu ayyuhā al-faẓẓu al-ghalīẓu innī ushabbihuka fī ḥusni ʿalāniyatika wa-qawlika wa-aqīsu qubḥa niyyatika wa-fiʿlika bi-al-bāzī maʿa al-ḥajali
sentences.l: And the fox said to him: O you the coarse, the harsh! I liken-you in the fairness of your outward-show and your speech, and I-measure the foulness of your intent and your deed, by the falcon with the partridge.
sentences.i: The fox said to him, “You coarse brute! In your fair outward show and your fine words, and in the foulness of your intent and your deeds, I can only compare you to the falcon and the partridge.”
sentences.n: The print has الثلعب, a misprint for الثعلب, corrected here. The fox's reply is the setup for a fable. faẓẓ and ghalīẓ, “rough, harsh”, a pair from the Qurʾān (3:159). ʿalāniya, “what is public, outward conduct”, against niyya, “inner intent”. Both verbs, ushabbihu and aqīsu, are completed by bi-al-bāzī, “to the falcon”: qāsa … bi-, “to measure one thing against another”. The shaddas in ايّها, الفظّ and انّي are the print's own.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الذِّئْبُ وَكَيْفَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-dhiʾbu wa-kayfa dhālika
sentences.l: And the wolf said: And how (was) that?
sentences.i: “And how was that?” asked the wolf.
sentences.n: wa-kayfa dhālika, “and how was that?”, is the stock question that calls up a tale in the Nights.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الثَّعْلَبُ دَخَلْتُ يَوْمًا كَرْمًا لِآكُلَ مِنْ عِنَبِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-thaʿlabu dakhaltu yawman karman li-ākula min ʿinabihi
sentences.l: And the fox said: I-entered one-day a vineyard to-eat of its grapes.
sentences.i: The fox said, “One day I went into a vineyard to eat some of its grapes.
sentences.n: li-ākula, “so that I might eat”: li- of purpose with the subjunctive. The madda in لآكل is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا أَنَا فِيهِ إِذْ رَأَيْتُ بَأزِيًا انْقَضَّ عَلَى حَجَلٍ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā anā fīhi idh raʾaytu bāziyan inqaḍḍa ʿalā ḥajalin
sentences.l: And while I (was) in-it, behold, I-saw a falcon (that) swooped upon a partridge.
sentences.i: While I was there, I saw a falcon swoop down on a partridge.
sentences.n: baynamā … idh, “while … suddenly”. The print sets a hamza on the alif of bāzī, “falcon”, بأزيا, as it does twice more in this tale (البأزي); it is kept, but the word is bāzī, and it is read so. inqaḍḍa ʿalā, “to swoop down on”: the shadda is the print's own. ḥajal is properly the collective “partridges”, used here of a single bird.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَلِقَهُ وَاقْتَنَصَهُ انْفَلَتَ مِنْهُ الْحَجَلُ وَدَخَلَ وَكْرَهُ وَاخْتَفَى فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿaliqahu wa-iqtanaṣahu infalata minhu al-ḥajalu wa-dakhala wakrahu wa-ikhtafā fīhi
sentences.l: And when it caught-hold-of-it and seized-it, the partridge slipped-away from-it, and entered its nest and hid in-it.
sentences.i: But just as he had caught and seized it, the partridge slipped out of his grip, went into its nest and hid there.
sentences.n: ʿaliqa, “to catch hold of, cling to”; iqtanaṣa, “to snatch as prey”. infalata, “to slip loose, escape”. The pointing of وَكْره is partly the print's.

sentences.t: فَتَبِعَهُ الْبَأزِي وَنَادَاهُ أَيُّهَا الْجَافِلُ إِنِّي رَأَيْتُكَ فِي الْبَرِّيَّةِ جَائِعًا فَرَحِمْتُكَ وَالْتَقَطْتُ لَكَ حَبًّا وَأَمْسَكْتُكَ لِنَأْكُلَ
sentences.tr: fa-tabiʿahu al-bāzī wa-nādāhu ayyuhā al-jāfilu innī raʾaytuka fī al-barriyyati jāʾiʿan fa-raḥimtuka wa-iltaqaṭtu laka ḥabban wa-amsaktuka li-naʾkula
sentences.l: And the falcon followed it and called-to-it: O you the one-who-bolted, I saw-you in the open-country hungry, and I-pitied-you, and picked-up for you grain, and held-you so-that we-might-eat.
sentences.i: The falcon followed and called to him, ‘You runaway! I saw you out in the wilds, hungry, and took pity on you; I gathered grain for you, and I only took hold of you so that we might eat together.
sentences.n: The print again has البأزي with a hamza on the alif; read al-bāzī. jāfil, “one who takes fright and bolts”. barriyya, “open country, the wild”. The ḍamma on التقطتُ, the shadda on حبّا and the hamza on لنأكل are the print's own.

sentences.t: فَهَرَبْتَ مِنِّي وَ لَمْ أَعْرِفْ لِهُرُوبِكَ وَجْهًا إِلَّا الْحِرْمَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-harabta minnī wa-lam aʿrif li-hurūbika wajhan illā al-ḥirmāna
sentences.l: And you-fled from-me, and I-did-not know for your fleeing a reason except the deprivation.
sentences.i: But you fled from me, and I can see no reason for your flight except that you would rob yourself of what was yours.
sentences.n: The print sets the wa- of wa-lam at the end of one line and lam on the next, as two separate words; the spacing is kept. wajh, “face”, here “aspect, reason”. ḥirmān, “deprivation, going without”: running away gets you nothing. The shadda on الّا is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَاظْهَرْ وَخُذْ مَا آتَيْتُكَ بِهِ مِنَ الْحَبِّ فَكُلْهُ هَنِيأً مَرِيأً
sentences.tr: fa-iẓhar wa-khudh mā ātaytuka bihi mina al-ḥabbi fa-kulhu hanīʾan marīʾan
sentences.l: So come-out and take what I-have-brought-you with-it of the grain, and eat-it, wholesome, healthful.
sentences.i: So come out, take the grain I have brought you, and eat it, and may it do you good!’
sentences.n: ẓahara, “to come out, show oneself”. The print writes آتيتك with madda, which would be ātaytuka, “I gave you”; with bihi the expected verb is ataytuka bihi, “I brought you”, as the partridge says below. The print's spelling is kept and read as written; the sense is the same. hanīʾan marīʾan, “with health and good digestion!”, the stock wish over food, here spelt هنيأ مريأ with the hamza on the alif.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْحَجَلُ قَوْلَ الْبَأزِي صَدَّقَهُ وَخَرَجَ إِلَيْهِ فَأَنْشَبَ مَخَالِبَهُ فِيهِ وَمَكَّنَهَا مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-ḥajalu qawla al-bāzī ṣaddaqahu wa-kharaja ilayhi fa-anshaba makhālibahu fīhi wa-makkanahā minhu
sentences.l: And when the partridge heard the speech of the falcon, it believed-him and came-out to-him; and he sank his talons in-it and made-them-fast in-it.
sentences.i: When the partridge heard the falcon's words, he believed him and came out to him; and the falcon sank his talons into him and gripped him fast.
sentences.n: anshaba, “to fix, drive in (claws)”; makkana … min, “to make firm, give a hold on”. The shadda on ومكّنها is the print's own. Read البأزي as al-bāzī, as before.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْحَجَلُ أَهَذَا الَّذِى ذَكَرْتَ أَنَّكَ أَتَيْتَ لِي بِهِ مِنَ الْبَرِّيَّةِ وَقُلْتَ لِي كُلْهُ هَنِيأً مَرِيأً فَكَذَبْتَ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-ḥajalu a-hādhā alladhī dhakarta annaka atayta lī bihi mina al-barriyyati wa-qulta lī kulhu hanīʾan marīʾan fa-kadhabta ʿalayya
sentences.l: And the partridge said to him: Is-this what you-mentioned that you brought for me from the open-country, and you-said to-me: Eat-it, wholesome, healthful? So you-lied to-me.
sentences.i: The partridge said to him, ‘Is this what you told me you had brought me from the wilds, when you said, “Eat it, and may it do you good”? You lied to me.
sentences.n: The print has البزية, a misprint for البرية, corrected here. atā lī bihi, “you brought it for me”: atā bi-, “to bring”. The fatḥas on ذكرتَ and قلتَ and the shadda on عليّ are the print's own. kadhaba ʿalā, “to lie to”.

sentences.t: جَعَلَ اللَّهُ مَا تَأْكُلُهُ مِنْ لَحْمِي فِي جَوْفِكَ سُمًّا قَاتِلًا
sentences.tr: jaʿala allāhu mā taʾkuluhu min laḥmī fī jawfika summan qātilan
sentences.l: May-God-make what you-eat of my flesh in your belly a poison killing!
sentences.i: May God turn whatever you eat of my flesh into deadly poison in your belly!’
sentences.n: jaʿala in the perfect, used as a wish or curse: “may God make …”. jaʿala … summan, “to make (something) into poison”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَكَلَهُ وَقَعَ رِيشُهُ وَسَقَطَتْ قُوَّتُهُ وَمَاتَ لِوَقْتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā akalahu waqaʿa rīshuhu wa-saqaṭat quwwatuhu wa-māta li-waqtihi
sentences.l: And when he ate-him, his feathers fell, and his strength collapsed, and he-died at-his-time (on the spot).
sentences.i: When the falcon had eaten him, his feathers fell out, his strength failed, and he died on the spot.
sentences.n: li-waqtihi, “at its time”: then and there.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ الثَّعْلَبُ اعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الذِّئْبُ أَنَّ مَنْ حَفَرَ لِأَخِيهِ قَلِيبًا وَقَعَ فِيهِ قَرِيبًا وَأَنْتَ غَدَرْتَ بِي أَوَّلًا
sentences.tr: thumma qāla lahu al-thaʿlabu iʿlam ayyuhā al-dhiʾbu anna man ḥafara li-akhīhi qalīban waqaʿa fīhi qarīban wa-anta ghadarta bī awwalan
sentences.l: Then the fox said to him: Know, O you the wolf, that whoever digs for his brother a well falls into-it soon; and you betrayed me first.
sentences.i: Then the fox said to him, “Know, wolf, that whoever digs a pit for his brother will soon fall into it himself; and it was you who first betrayed me.”
sentences.n: A proverb, in rhyme: man ḥafara li-akhīhi qalīban waqaʿa fīhi qarīban. qalīb, “a well, an old unlined well”. ghadara bi-, “to betray”. The shadda on اوّلا is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الذِّئْبُ لِلثَّعْلَبِ دَعْنِي مِنْ هَذَا الْمَقَالِ وَضَرْبِ الْأَمْثَالِ وَلَا تَذْكُرْ لِي مَا سَلَفَ مِنِّي مِنْ قَبِيحِ الْفِعَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-dhiʾbu li-al-thaʿlabi daʿnī min hādhā al-maqāli wa-ḍarbi al-amthāli wa-lā tadhkur lī mā salafa minnī min qabīḥi al-fiʿāli
sentences.l: And the wolf said to the fox: Leave-me from this talk and the striking of the parables, and do-not mention to me what went-before from me of the foulness of the deeds.
sentences.i: The wolf said to the fox, “Spare me this talk and these parables, and do not remind me of my past foul deeds.
sentences.n: daʿnī min, “leave me out of, spare me”. ḍaraba mathalan, “to strike a parable”: to tell one. al-maqāl / al-amthāl / al-fiʿāl rhyme.

sentences.t: يَكْفِينِي مَا أَنَا فِيهِ مِنْ سُوءِ الْحَالِ لِأَنِّي قَدْ حَصَلْتُ فِي مَوْضِعٍ يَرْثِي لِي مِنْهَا الْعَدُوُّ فَضْلًا عَنِ الصَّدِيقِ
sentences.tr: yakfīnī mā anā fīhi min sūʾi al-ḥāli li-annī qad ḥaṣaltu fī mawḍiʿin yarthī lī minhā al-ʿaduwwu faḍlan ʿani al-ṣadīqi
sentences.l: Sufficient-for-me (is) what I (am) in-it of the badness of the state; because I have-landed in a place (that) the enemy pities me from-it, let-alone the friend.
sentences.i: The wretched state I am in is enough for me; I have come to such a pass that even an enemy would pity me, let alone a friend.
sentences.n: ḥaṣala fī, “to end up in, find oneself in”. rathā li-, “to feel pity for”. minhā, “from it”, is feminine though mawḍiʿ, “place”, is masculine: perhaps thought of as the pit, ḥufra, or as the plight, ḥāl; such loose agreement is common in Middle Arabic. faḍlan ʿan, “let alone, not to mention”.

sentences.t: وَاصْنَعْ لِي حِيلَةً أَتَخَلَّصُ بِهَا وَكُنْ فِيهَا غِيَاثِي
sentences.tr: wa-iṣnaʿ lī ḥīlatan atakhallaṣu bihā wa-kun fīhā ghiyāthī
sentences.l: And make for-me a stratagem (by which) I-may-escape with-it, and be in-it my rescue.
sentences.i: Devise me some stratagem by which I can get free, and be my rescuer in it.
sentences.n: atakhallaṣu bihā, “by which I may get free”, describes ḥīla, with no alladhī after the indefinite noun. ghiyāth, “succour, rescue”. The shadda on اتخلّص is the print's own.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ كَانَ عَلَيْكَ فِي ذَلِكَ مَشَقَّةٌ فَقَدْ يَتَحَمَّلُ الصَّدِيقُ لِصَدِيقِهِ أَشَدَّ النَّصَبِ وَيُخَاطِرُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِيمَا فِيهِ نَجَاتُهُ مِنَ الْعَطَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-in kāna ʿalayka fī dhālika mashaqqatun fa-qad yataḥammalu al-ṣadīqu li-ṣadīqihi ashadda al-naṣabi wa-yukhāṭiru bi-nafsihi fīmā fīhi najātuhu mina al-ʿaṭabi
sentences.l: And if there-is on-you in that a hardship, (well,) the friend will bear for his friend the hardest of the toil, and risk his life in what in-it (is) his salvation from the ruin.
sentences.i: And if it costs you some trouble, a friend will often bear the hardest toil for his friend, and risk his own life to save him from ruin.
sentences.n: qad with the imperfect, “sometimes, often”. khāṭara bi-nafsihi, “to stake one's life”. najātuhu, “his rescue”: the friend's, not the rescuer's. al-naṣab / al-ʿaṭab rhyme. The shadda on يتحمّل is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَقَدْ قِيلَ إِنَّ الصَّدِيقَ الشَّفِيقَ خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْأَخِ الشَّقِيقِ
