sentences.tr: fa-qad qīla inna al-ṣadīqa al-shafīqa khayrun mina al-akhi al-shaqīqi
sentences.l: For it has-been-said: The friend, the tender, (is) better than the brother, the full (brother).
sentences.i: For it has been said, ‘A loving friend is better than a full brother.’
sentences.n: A rhyming saying: shafīq, “tender, solicitous”, and shaqīq, “full brother, of the same father and mother”, differ by a single letter.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ تَسَبَّبْتَ فِى نَجَاتِي وَنَجَوْتُ لَأَجْمَعَنَّ لَكَ مِنَ الْآلَةِ مَايَكُونُ لَكَ عُدَّةً
sentences.tr: fa-in tasabbabta fī najātī wa-najawtu la-ajmaʿanna laka mina al-ālati mā yakūnu laka ʿuddatan
sentences.l: So if you-contrive my rescue and I-escape, I-will-surely-gather for you of the gear what will-be for you a provision.
sentences.i: If you find a way to rescue me and I escape, I swear I will gather you such gear as will stand you in good stead,
sentences.n: la-ajmaʿanna, “I will surely gather”, the oath form: la- with the energetic -anna. āla, “gear, tools, equipment”; ʿudda, “store, equipment kept ready”. The fatḥa on تسببتَ, the ḍamma on نجوتُ, the madda in الآلة and the shadda on عدّة are the print's own. The print runs mā yakūnu together as مايكون; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ لَأُ عَلِّمَنَّكَ مِنَ الْحِيَلِ الْغَرِيبَةِ مَاتَفْتَحُ بِهِ الْكُرُومَ الْخَصِبَةَ وَتَجْنِى الْأَشْجَارَ الْمُثْمِرَةَ فَطِبْ نَفْسًا وَقَرَّ عَيْنًا
sentences.tr: thumma la-uʿallimannaka mina al-ḥiyali al-gharībati mā taftaḥu bihi al-kurūma al-khaṣibata wa-tajnī al-ashjāra al-muthmirata fa-ṭib nafsan wa-qarra ʿaynan
sentences.l: Then I-will-surely-teach-you of the stratagems, the strange, what you-will-open with-it the vineyards, the fertile, and you-will-pick the trees, the fruit-bearing. So be-good of-soul and be-cool of-eye!
sentences.i: and then I will teach you such rare tricks as will open the rich vineyards to you and let you strip the fruit trees. So be of good heart, and let your eye be glad!”
sentences.n: la-uʿallimannaka, “I will surely teach you”, another oath form, which the print splits in two as لا علمنك; the spacing is kept. janā, “to gather (fruit)”: tajnī al-ashjāra, “you will pick the trees”, spelt with alif maqṣūra. ṭib nafsan wa-qarra ʿaynan, “be of good cheer”: a cool eye, qurrat al-ʿayn, is the Arabic image of contentment; the shadda on قرّ is the print's own. The print runs mā taftaḥu together as ماتفتح; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الثَّعْلَبُ وَهُوَ يَضْحَكُ مَا أَحْسَنَ مَا قَالَتْهُ الْعُلَمَاءُ فِي كَثِيرِ الْجَهْلِ مِثْلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-thaʿlabu wa-huwa yaḍḥaku mā aḥsana mā qālathu al-ʿulamāʾu fī kathīri al-jahli mithlika
sentences.l: And the fox said to-him, and he (was) laughing: How fine (is) what the learned-men said about (one) much-of ignorance like-you!
sentences.i: The fox laughed and said to him, “How well the learned have spoken of those as full of ignorance as you!”
sentences.n: mā aḥsana, “how fine!”, the verb of wonder (taʿajjub), with the thing admired in the accusative: mā aḥsana mā qālathu, “how fine is what they said”. kathīr al-jahl, “much of ignorance”, an adjective governing a noun: “abounding in ignorance”. al-ʿulamāʾ takes a feminine verb, qālathu, as broken plurals may.

sentences.t: قَالَ الذِّئْبُ وَمَا قَالَتِ الْعُلَمَاءُ
sentences.tr: qāla al-dhiʾbu wa-mā qālati al-ʿulamāʾu
sentences.l: Said the wolf: And what did the learned-men say?
sentences.i: “And what did the learned say?” asked the wolf.

sentences.t: قَالَ الثَّعْلَبُ ذَكَرَ الْعُلَمَاءُ أَنَّ الْغَلِيظَ الْجُثَّةِ الْغَلِيظَ الطَّبْعِ يَكُونُ بَعِيدًا مِنَ الْعَقْلِ قَرِيبًا مِنَ الْجَهْلِ
sentences.tr: qāla al-thaʿlabu dhakara al-ʿulamāʾu anna al-ghalīẓa al-juththati al-ghalīẓa al-ṭabʿi yakūnu baʿīdan mina al-ʿaqli qarīban mina al-jahli
sentences.l: Said the fox: The learned-men mentioned that the thick of body, the thick of nature, is far from the reason, near to the ignorance.
sentences.i: The fox said, “The learned say that one who is gross of body and gross of nature is far from good sense and near to folly.
sentences.n: al-ghalīẓ al-juththa, al-ghalīẓ al-ṭabʿ, “the thick of body, the thick of nature”: an adjective with the article governing a noun, the “improper annexation”. baʿīdan … qarīban, a balanced pair: far from reason, near to ignorance.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا قَوْلُكَ أَيُّهَا الْمَغْرُورُ الْمَاكِرُ الْأَحْمَقُ قَدْ يَتَحَمَّلُ الصَّدِيقُ الْمَشَقَّةَ فِي تَخْلِيصِ صَدِيقِهِ صَحِيحٌ كَمَا ذَكَرْتَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā qawluka ayyuhā al-maghrūru al-mākiru al-aḥmaqu qad yataḥammalu al-ṣadīqu al-mashaqqata fī takhlīṣi ṣadīqihi ṣaḥīḥun kamā dhakarta
sentences.l: And as-for your saying, O you the deluded, the wily, the foolish, “The friend may bear the hardship in the rescuing of his friend”, (it is) true as you mentioned,
sentences.i: As for what you said, you deluded, crafty fool, that a friend will sometimes bear hardship to rescue his friend: that is true, as you say,
sentences.n: ammā, “as for”, is answered in Classical Arabic by fa- on the next clause (fa-ṣaḥīḥun); the print has ṣaḥīḥun with no fa-, a looseness common in this Arabic. The fox quotes the wolf's own maxim back at him.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ عَرِّفْنِي بِجَهْلِكَ وَقِلَّةِ عَقْلِكَ كَيْفَ أُصَادِقُكَ مَعَ خِيَانَتِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin ʿarrifnī bi-jahlika wa-qillati ʿaqlika kayfa uṣādiquka maʿa khiyānatika
sentences.l: but make-known-to-me, with your ignorance and the littleness of your reason, how I-should-befriend-you with your treachery.
sentences.i: but tell me, in your ignorance and want of sense, how am I to be your friend when you are so treacherous?
sentences.n: The print has اصادتك, a misprint for اصادقك, corrected here. uṣādiquka, “I befriend you, I am a true friend to you”, from the same root as ṣadīq, “friend”. bi-jahlika, “with your ignorance”: the fox mocks the wolf for asking at all.

sentences.t: أَحَسِبْتَنِي لَكَ صَدِيقًا وَأَنَا لَكَ عَدُوٌّ شَامِتٌ وَهَذَا الْكَلَامُ أَشَدُّ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ وَرَشْقِ السِّهَامِ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْقِلُ
sentences.tr: a-ḥasibtanī laka ṣadīqan wa-anā laka ʿaduwwun shāmitun wa-hādhā al-kalāmu ashaddu mina al-qatli wa-rashqi al-sihāmi in kunta taʿqilu
sentences.l: Did-you-reckon-me to-you a friend, while I (am) to-you an enemy rejoicing-at-your-harm? And this speech (is) harder than the killing and the shooting of the arrows, if you were-understanding.
sentences.i: Did you take me for your friend, when I am your enemy and delight in your misfortune? These words are harder to bear than death or a volley of arrows, if you have the sense to understand them.
sentences.n: a- is the question prefix. ḥasiba, “to reckon, suppose”, takes two objects: “reckon me a friend”. shāmit, “one who rejoices at another's misfortune”; the same root gives tashmatu and al-shāmitīna below. rashq al-sihām, “the shooting of arrows”.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا قَوْلُكَ تَدْفَعُ لِي مِنَ الْآلَةِ مَا يَكُونُ عُدَّةً لِي وَتُعَلِّمُنِي مِنَ الْحِيَلِ مَا أَصِلُ بِهِ إِلَى الْكُرُومِ الْمُخْصِبَةِ وَأَجْتَنِي بِهِ الْأَشْجَارَ الْمُثْمِرَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā qawluka tadfaʿu lī mina al-ālati mā yakūnu ʿuddatan lī wa-tuʿallimunī mina al-ḥiyali mā aṣilu bihi ilā al-kurūmi al-mukhṣibati wa-ajtanī bihi al-ashjāra al-muthmirata
sentences.l: And as-for your saying (that) you-will-hand to-me of the gear what will-be equipment for-me, and will-teach-me of the stratagems what I-may-reach by-it to the vineyards, the fertile ones, and gather by-it the trees, the fruit-bearing ones,
sentences.i: And as for your promise to give me gear to equip me and to teach me tricks by which I might reach the rich vineyards and gather from the fruit-laden trees:
sentences.n: The fox repeats the wolf's offer in indirect form: tadfaʿu lī, “you will hand me”, is the wolf's “I will hand you” turned round. āla, “gear, implements”; ʿudda, “equipment, provision”. ijtanā, “to gather (fruit)”, here with the trees themselves as object. The hamza in الآلة is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَمَالَكَ أَيُّهَا الْمُخَادِعُ الْغَادِرُ لَا تَعْرِفُ لَكَ حِيلَةً تَتَخَلَّصُ بِهَا مِنَ الْهَلَاكِ
sentences.tr: fa-mā laka ayyuhā al-mukhādiʿu al-ghādiru lā taʿrifu laka ḥīlatan tatakhallaṣu bihā mina al-halāki
sentences.l: Then what-is-with-you, O you the cheat, the betrayer, (that) you-do-not know for-yourself a stratagem you-may-get-free by-it from the perishing?
sentences.i: Then what ails you, you cheat and traitor, that you know no trick to save yourself from destruction?
sentences.n: mā laka, “what is (the matter) with you?”, followed by a clause, “that you do not …”; the print runs it together as مالك, kept here. ḥīlatan tatakhallaṣu bihā, a relative clause without a pronoun after an indefinite noun: “a trick (by which) you might escape”.

sentences.t: فَمَا أَبْعَدَكَ مِنَ الْمَنْفَعَةِ لِنَفْسِكَ وَمَا أَبْعَدَنِي مِنَ الْقَبُولِ لِنَصِيحَتِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-mā abʿadaka mina al-manfaʿati li-nafsika wa-mā abʿadanī mina al-qabūli li-naṣīḥatika
sentences.l: So how far you (are) from the profit for yourself, and how far I (am) from the accepting of your counsel!
sentences.i: How far you are from doing yourself any good, and how far am I from taking your advice!
sentences.n: Two exclamations of wonder, mā abʿadaka … mā abʿadanī, “how far you are … how far I am”, set side by side, with nafsika and naṣīḥatika closing them.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ كَانَ عِنْدَكَ حِيلَةٌ فَتَحَيَّلْ لِنَفْسِكَ فِى الْخَلَاصِ مِنْ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ الَّذِي أَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ أَنْ يُبْعِدَ خَلَاصَكَ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-in kāna ʿindaka ḥīlatun fa-taḥayyal li-nafsika fī al-khalāṣi min hādhā al-amri alladhī asʾalu allāha an yubʿida khalāṣaka minhu
sentences.l: So if there-is with-you a stratagem, then contrive for yourself in the escaping from this matter, which I-ask God that He-make-far your escaping from-it.
sentences.i: If you have any trick, then use it to get yourself out of this plight, from which I pray God you may never escape.
sentences.n: kāna ʿindaka ḥīlatun: a masculine verb before a feminine subject, allowed when other words stand between them. taḥayyala, “to use a stratagem, contrive”, from the same root as ḥīla, “trick”. The hamza in اسأل is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَانْظُرْ أَيُّهَا الْجَاهِلُ إِنْ كَانَ عِنْدَكَ حِيلَةٌ فَخَلِّصْ نَفْسَكَ بِهَا مِنَ الْقَتْلِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَبْذُلَ التَّعْلِيمَ لِغَيْرِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-unẓur ayyuhā al-jāhilu in kāna ʿindaka ḥīlatun fa-khalliṣ nafsaka bihā mina al-qatli qabla an tabdhula al-taʿlīma li-ghayrika
sentences.l: So look, O you the ignorant, if there-is with-you a stratagem, then free yourself by-it from the killing before that you-give-freely the teaching to other-than-you.
sentences.i: Look to it, you fool: if you have a trick, save yourself from death with it before you go offering lessons to others.
sentences.n: badhala, “to give freely, lavish”. The shadda in فخلّص is the print's own.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنَّكَ مِثْلُ إِنْسَانٍ نَابَهُ مَرَضٌ فَأَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ مَرِيضٌ بِمِثْلِ مَرَضِهِ لِيُدَاوِيَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lākinnaka mithlu insānin nābahu maraḍun fa-atāhu rajulun marīḍun bi-mithli maraḍihi li-yudāwiyahu
sentences.l: But you (are) like a person (whom) a sickness befell, and there-came-to-him a man sick with the like of his sickness, to treat-him.
sentences.i: But you are like a man who fell ill, and another man, sick with the same disease, came to cure him.
sentences.n: nābahu, “befell him”, from nāba, yanūbu, used of misfortunes that come upon one. insānin nābahu, again a relative clause without a pronoun after an indefinite noun.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ أُدَاوِيَكَ مِنْ مَرَضِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu hal laka an udāwiyaka min maraḍika
sentences.l: And he said to-him: Is (there) for-you that I-treat-you from your sickness?
sentences.i: He said to him, ‘Would you like me to cure you of your sickness?’
sentences.n: hal laka an …, “have you (a wish) that …?”, the polite way of offering something.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الرَّجُلُ هَلْ لَابَدَأْتَ بِنَفْسِكَ بِالْمُدَاوَاةِ فَخَلَّاهُ وَانْصَرَفَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-rajulu hal lā badaʾta bi-nafsika bi-al-mudāwāti fa-khallāhu wa-inṣarafa
sentences.l: And the man said to-him: Why not have-you-begun with yourself with the treating? So he left-him and went-away.
sentences.i: The man answered, ‘Why have you not begun by treating yourself?’ So he left him alone and went away.
sentences.n: hal lā, for hallā, “why not?”, with a past verb a reproach: “why did you not …?” The print sets هل apart and runs لا into the verb, لابدأت; the spacing is kept, and the hamza in it is the print's own. A form of the old saying “Physician, heal yourself”.

sentences.t: وَأَنْتَ أَيُّهَا الذِّئْبُ الْجَاهِلُ كَذَلِكَ فَالْزَمْ مَكَانَكَ وَاصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا أَصَابَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-anta ayyuhā al-dhiʾbu al-jāhilu ka-dhālika fa-ilzam makānaka wa-iṣbir ʿalā mā aṣābaka
sentences.l: And you, O you the wolf, the ignorant, (are) like-that; so keep-to your place and be-patient upon what has-struck-you.
sentences.i: And you, ignorant wolf, are just the same. So stay where you are, and bear what has befallen you with patience.”
sentences.n: lazima, “to keep to, stay fixed in”. ṣabara ʿalā, “to bear patiently”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الذِّئْبُ كَلَامَ الثَّعْلَبِ عَلِمَ أَنَّهُ لَاخَيْرَ لَهُ عِنْدَهُ فَبَكَى عَلَى نَفْسِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-dhiʾbu kalāma al-thaʿlabi ʿalima annahu lā khayra lahu ʿindahu fa-bakā ʿalā nafsihi
sentences.l: And when the wolf heard the speech of the fox, he knew that there-is-no good for-him with-him, and he wept over himself.
sentences.i: When the wolf heard the fox's words, he knew there was no good to be had from him, and he wept for himself.
sentences.n: lā khayra, “no good”, lā of absolute negation with its noun in the accusative; the print runs the two words together, لاخير, and the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ قَدْ كُنْتُ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ أَمْرِي
sentences.tr: wa-qāla qad kuntu fī ghaflatin min amrī
sentences.l: And he said: I was in heedlessness of my affair.
sentences.i: He said, “I have been heedless of my own state.
sentences.n: ghafla, “heedlessness”, the word of the preachers for a life lived without thought of God. The ḍamma on كنتُ is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ خَلَّصَنِي اللَّهُ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْكُرْبَةِ لَأَنُوبَنَّ مِنْ تَجَبُّرِي عَلَى مَنْ هُوَ أَضْعَفُ مِنِّي وَلَأَلْبَسَنَّ الصُّوفَ وَلَأَ صْعَدَنَّ عَلَى الْجَبَلِ ذَاكِرًا لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى خَائِفًا مِنْ عِقَابِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-in khallaṣanī allāhu min hādhihi al-kurbati la-anūbanna min tajabburī ʿalā man huwa aḍʿafu minnī wa-la-albasanna al-ṣūfa wa-la-aṣʿadanna ʿalā al-jabali dhākiran li-allāhi taʿālā khāʾifan min ʿiqābihi
sentences.l: So if God frees-me from this distress, I-shall-surely-turn-back from my tyrannising over whoever is weaker than-me, and I-shall-surely-put-on the wool, and I-shall-surely-climb upon the mountain, remembering God, (may He be) exalted, fearing His punishment,
sentences.i: If God delivers me from this distress, I will surely repent of my tyranny over those weaker than I, and put on wool, and go up into the mountains to call God Most High to mind and stand in fear of His punishment,
sentences.n: la-…-anna, the oath-form of the verb with la- of emphasis and the energetic ending: “I will surely …”. anāba and nāba, “to turn back (to God), repent”. Wearing wool (ṣūf) is the mark of the ascetic, the word from which ṣūfī is commonly derived; climbing the mountain means a hermit's life. The print splits the last verb, ولا صعدنّ, for wa-la-aṣʿadanna; the spacing is kept and the pointing runs across the gap. The fatḥa in لاَنوبنّ, the shaddas in تجبّري and the three verbs, and the tanwīn in ذاكرًا and shadda in للّه are the print's own.

sentences.t: وَأَعْتَزِلُ سَائِرَ الْوُحُوشِ وَلَأُ طْعِمَنَّ الْمُجَاهِدِينَ وَالْفُقَرَاءَ
sentences.tr: wa-aʿtazilu sāʾira al-wuḥūshi wa-la-uṭʿimanna al-mujāhidīna wa-al-fuqarāʾa
sentences.l: and I-shall-withdraw-from all the beasts, and I-shall-surely-feed the strivers and the poor.
sentences.i: and I will keep apart from all the other beasts, and feed those who strive in God's way, and the poor.”
sentences.n: aʿtazilu has no oath-ending, unlike the verbs around it; it is read here as a plain future, “and I will withdraw”. The print splits the last verb as it did before, ولا طعمن, for wa-la-uṭʿimanna; the spacing is kept. mujāhidūn, “strivers”, those who struggle in God's cause, whether at war or against the self; a wolf promising to feed them is part of the joke.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَكَى وَانْتَحَبَ فَرَقَّ لَهُ قَلْبُ الثَّعْلَبِ وَكَائِهِ لَمَّا سَمِعَ تَضَرُّعَهُ وَالْكَلَامَ الَّذِي يَدُلُّ عَلَى تَوْبَتِهِ مِنَ الْعُتُوِّ وَالتَّكَبُّرِ أَخَذَتْهُ الشَّفَقَةُ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma bakā wa-intaḥaba fa-raqqa lahu qalbu al-thaʿlabi wa-kāʾihi lammā samiʿa taḍarruʿahu wa-al-kalāma alladhī yadullu ʿalā tawbatihi mina al-ʿutuwwi wa-al-takabburi akhadhathu al-shafaqatu ʿalayhi
sentences.l: Then he wept and sobbed, and the heart of the fox softened toward-him, and [as-though], when he heard his humble-pleading and the speech which shows his repentance from the insolence and the arrogance, the pity for-him took-him.
sentences.i: Then he wept and sobbed aloud, and the fox's heart softened toward him; and it was as though, when he heard him pleading so humbly and speaking words that showed he repented of his insolence and pride, pity for him took hold of him.
sentences.n: The print has وكائه, which makes no word as it stands; it is probably وكأنه, wa-ka-annahu, “and (it was) as though”, and is translated so, but the letters are kept and pointed as printed. raqqa lahu qalbuhu, “his heart grew tender toward him”. ʿutuww, “insolence, haughty rebellion”. The shadda in فرقّ is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَوَثَبَ مِنْ فَرْحَتِهِ وَوَقَفَ عَلَى شَفِيرِ الْحُفْرَةِ ثُمَّ جَلَسَ عَلَى رِجْلَيْهِ وَأَدْلَى ذَنَبَهُ فِى الْحُفْرَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-wathaba min farḥatihi wa-waqafa ʿalā shafīri al-ḥufrati thumma jalasa ʿalā rijlayhi wa-adlā dhanabahu fī al-ḥufrati
sentences.l: And he leapt from his gladness, and stood upon the brink of the pit, then sat upon his (hind) legs and let-down his tail into the pit.
sentences.i: He leapt up for joy and stood on the edge of the pit; then he sat back on his haunches and let his tail down into it.
sentences.n: adlā, “to let down (a bucket into a well)”, the word used of drawing water: the fox lowers his tail like a well-rope.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ الذِّئْبُ وَمَدَّ يَدَهُ إِلَى ذَنَبِ الثَّعْلَبِ وَجَذَبَهُ إِلَيْهِ فَصَارَ فِى الْحُفْرَةِ مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma al-dhiʾbu wa-madda yadahu ilā dhanabi al-thaʿlabi wa-jadhabahu ilayhi fa-ṣāra fī al-ḥufrati maʿahu
sentences.l: And the wolf stood-up and stretched his paw to the tail of the fox and pulled-him to-himself, so he came-to-be in the pit with-him.
sentences.i: The wolf rose, reached for the fox's tail, and dragged him down, so that he too was in the pit with him.
sentences.n: yad, “hand”, used of an animal's forepaw. The shadda in ومدّ is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الذِّئْبُ أَيُّهَا الثَّعْلَبُ الْقَلِيلُ الرَّحْمَةِ كَيْفَ تَشْمَتُ بِي وَقَدْ كُنْتَ صَاحِبِي وَتَحْتَ قَهْرِي وَقَدْ وَقَعْتَ مَعِي فِى الْحُفْرَةِ وَتَعَجَّلَتْ لَكَ الْعُقُوبَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-dhiʾbu ayyuhā al-thaʿlabu al-qalīlu al-raḥmati kayfa tashmatu bī wa-qad kunta ṣāḥibī wa-taḥta qahrī wa-qad waqaʿta maʿī fī al-ḥufrati wa-taʿajjalat laka al-ʿuqūbatu
sentences.l: And the wolf said to-him: O you fox, the little of mercy, how (could) you-gloat over-me, when you were my companion and under my subjection? And you have fallen with-me into the pit, and the punishment has-hastened to-you.
sentences.i: Then the wolf said to him, “You pitiless fox, how could you gloat over me, when you were my companion and under my rule? Now you have fallen into the pit with me, and your punishment has come quickly.
sentences.n: shamita bi-, “to rejoice at (someone's) misfortune”. qahr, “subjection, overpowering”: taḥta qahrī, “in my power”. The shadda in وتعجّلت is the print's own.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قَالَتِ الْحُكَمَاءُ لَوْ عَايَرَ أَحَدُكُمْ أَخَاهُ بِرَضَاعِ كَلْبَةٍ لَارْتَضَعَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qad qālati al-ḥukamāʾu law ʿāyara aḥadukum akhāhu bi-raḍāʿi kalbatin la-irtaḍaʿahā
sentences.l: And the wise-men have said: If one-of-you reproached his brother with sucking a bitch, he-would-suck-her (himself).
sentences.i: The sages have said: If one of you taunted his brother with having been suckled by a bitch, he would come to suck her himself.
sentences.n: A saying: whoever mocks another for a disgrace will fall into the same disgrace. ʿāyara bi-, “to taunt (someone) with”. la-, after law, introduces the result: “he would …”.

sentences.t: وَمَا أَحْسَنَ قَوْلَ الشَّاعِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā aḥsana qawla al-shāʿiri
sentences.l: And how fine (is) the saying of the poet:
sentences.i: How well the poet put it:

sentences.t:
اِذَا مَا الدَّهْرُ جَرَّ عَلَى اُنَاسٍ * كَلَاكِلُهُ اَنَاخَ بِاَخَرِيْنَا
فَقُلْ للشَّامِتِيْنَ بِنَا اَفِيْقُوْا * سَيَلْقَى الشَّامِتُوْنَ كَمَا لَقِيْنَا
sentences.tr:
idhā mā al-dahru jarra ʿalā unāsin * kalākiluhu anākha bi-akharīnā
fa-qul li-al-shāmitīna binā afīqū * sa-yalqā al-shāmitūna kamā laqīnā
sentences.l:
When the time drags upon (some) people * its breasts, it kneels-down upon others.
So say to the gloaters over-us: Wake-up! * The gloaters will-meet as we have-met.
sentences.i:
When fortune drags its breast over one people, * it soon kneels down upon another.
So tell those who gloat over us: Wake up! * The gloaters will meet the fate we met.
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own. Fortune is pictured as a camel that crushes those beneath it as it settles: kalākil, “breasts” (of a camel), anākha, “to kneel (a camel) down”. The line is usually quoted with kalākilahu in the accusative, the object of jarra; the print points kalākiluhu, nominative, and its vowel is kept. بِاَخَرِيْنَا is the print's spelling of bi-ākharīna, “upon others”, without the madda. The lines are old and widely quoted; the attribution varies, al-Farazdaq being the name most often given.

sentences.t: وَالْمَوْتُ فِي جَمْعٍ أَحْسَنُ أَشْيَاءَ فَلَأُ عَجِّلَنَّ قَتْلَكَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَرَى قَتْلِي
sentences.tr: wa-al-mawtu fī jamʿin aḥsanu ashyāʾa fa-la-uʿajjilanna qatlaka qabla an tarā qatlī
sentences.l: And the death in a company (is) the finest of things; so I-shall-surely-hasten your killing before that you-see my killing.
sentences.i: Death in company is the best of things, so I will be sure to kill you first, before you can see me die.”
sentences.n: “Death in company” echoes the proverb al-mawtu maʿa al-jamāʿati raḥmatun, “death shared with others is a mercy”. aḥsanu ashyāʾa, “the best of things”, with an indefinite plural after the elative. The print splits the verb, فلا عجّلن, for fa-la-uʿajjilanna, as it split the wolf's vows; the spacing is kept, and the shadda is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الثَّعْلَبُ فِي نَفْسِهِ آهٍ آهٍ إِنِّي وَقَعْتُ مَعَ هَذَا الْجَبَّارِ وَهَذَا الْحَالُ يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى الْمَكْرِ وَالْخِدَاعِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-thaʿlabu fī nafsihi āhin āhin innī waqaʿtu maʿa hādhā al-jabbāri wa-hādhā al-ḥālu yaḥtāju ilā al-makri wa-al-khidāʿi
sentences.l: And the fox said in himself: Ah, ah! I have-fallen with this tyrant, and this state needs the cunning and the deceit.
sentences.i: The fox said to himself, “Alas, alas! I have fallen in with this tyrant, and this plight calls for cunning and deceit.
sentences.n: The print has اى, a misprint for الى, corrected here. āhin, “ah! alas!”, a cry of pain; the madda is the print's own. ḥāl, “state”, is often feminine; here it takes the masculine hādhā.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قِيلَ إِنَّ الْمَرْأَةَ تَصُوغُ حُلِيَّهَا لِيَوْمِ الزِّينَةِ وَفِى الْمَثَلِ مَا ادَّخَرْتُكِ يَا دَمْعَتِي إِلَّا لِشِدَّتِي
sentences.tr: wa-qad qīla inna al-marʾata taṣūghu ḥuliyyahā li-yawmi al-zīnati wa-fī al-mathali mā iddakhartuki yā damʿatī illā li-shiddatī
sentences.l: And it has been said: The woman fashions her ornaments for the day of the adornment. And in the proverb: I-did-not store-you-up, O my tear, except for my hardship.
sentences.i: It is said that a woman has her jewels made for the festal day; and the proverb says, ‘I kept you back, my tear, only for my day of trouble.’
sentences.n: Two sayings with one sense: what is stored up is meant for the day it is needed, and that day has come. ṣāgha, “to work (gold or silver), fashion jewellery”. yawm al-zīna, “the day of adornment”, a feast-day. iddakhara, “to lay by, store up”; mā … illā, “only”. The hamza in المرأة is the print's own.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ لَمْ أَتَحَيَّلْ فِي أَمْرِ هَذَا الْوَحْشِ الظَّالِمِ هَلَكْتُ لَا مَحَالَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-in lam ataḥayyal fī amri hādhā al-waḥshi al-ẓālimi halaktu lā maḥālata
sentences.l: And if I-do-not contrive in the matter of this beast, the wrongdoer, I-shall-have-perished, no escaping.
sentences.i: If I find no trick to deal with this cruel beast, I am lost beyond all doubt.
sentences.n: halaktu, a past verb answering in, “if”, read as future: “I shall perish”. lā maḥālata, “there is no avoiding (it)”, that is, “inevitably”.

sentences.t: وَمَا أَحْسَنَ قَوْلَ الشَّاعِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā aḥsana qawla al-shāʿiri
sentences.l: And how fine (is) the saying of the poet:
sentences.i: How well the poet put it:

sentences.t:
عِشْ بِالْخِدَاعِ فَاَنْتَ فِيْ * زَمَنٍ بَنُوْهُ كَاُسْدِ بِيْشَهْ
وَاَدِرْ قَنَاةَ الْمَكْرِ حَتَّى * تَسْتَدِيْرُ رَحَى الْمَعِيْشَهْ
وَاجْنِ الثِّمَارَ فَاِنْ تَفُتْـ * ـكَ فَرِّضْ نَفْسَكَ بِالْحَشِيْشَهْ
sentences.tr:
ʿish bi-al-khidāʿi fa-anta fī * zamanin banūhu ka-usdi bīshah
wa-adir qanāta al-makri ḥattā * tastadīru raḥā al-maʿīshah
wa-ijni al-thimāra fa-in tafut- * -ka farriḍ nafsaka bi-al-ḥashīshah
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own. Bīsha, a valley in western Arabia famed in poetry for its lions. raḥā, “millstone”: keep cunning turning and your bread will be ground. The last line splits tafutka, “escapes you”, across the hemistichs, marked in print with a stretching stroke. فَرِّضْ is doubtful: as printed it would be farriḍ, “apportion”, which gives no clear sense; the expected word is probably فَرَضِّ, fa-raḍḍi, “then content (your soul)”, and the translation follows that sense. The rhyme in -īshah keeps the pausal hāʾ.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الثَّعْلَبَ قَالَ لِلذِّئْبِ لَا تَعْجَلْ عَلَيَّ بِالْقَتْلِ فَلَيْسَ هَذَا جَزَائِي فَتَنَدَّمَ أَيُّهَا الْوَحْشُ الصِّنْدِيدُ صَاحِبُ الْقُوَّةِ وَالْبَأْسِ الشَّدِيدِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-thaʿlaba qāla li-al-dhiʾbi lā taʿjal ʿalayya bi-al-qatli fa-laysa hādhā jazāʾī fa-tanaddama ayyuhā al-waḥshu al-ṣindīdu ṣāḥibu al-quwwati wa-al-baʾsi al-shadīdi
sentences.l: Then the fox said to the wolf: Do-not hasten upon-me with the killing, for this is-not my reward, lest you-regret, O you the beast, the mighty-chief, the possessor of the strength and the valour, the severe.
sentences.i: Then the fox said to the wolf, “Do not be in a hurry to kill me, for I have not deserved it, and you will be sorry for it, you mighty beast, lord of strength and fierce valour.
sentences.n: fa-tanaddama, subjunctive after fa- in answer to a prohibition, “lest you regret”; tanaddama stands for tatanaddama, one tāʾ of the form V verb dropped. ṣindīd, “brave chief, mighty one”, rhymes with shadīd: the fox flatters in sajʿ. The shaddas in عليّ, فتندّم and ايّها, and the hamza in والبأس, are the print's own.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ تَمَهَّلْتَ وَأَمْعَنْتَ النَّظَرَ فِيمَا أَحْكِيهِ لَكَ عَرَفْتَ قَصْدِي الَّذِي قَصَدْتُهُ وَإِنْ عَجِلْتَ بِقَتْلِي فَلَا يَحْصُلُ فِي يَدِكَ شَيْءٌ وَنَمُوتُ جَمِيعًا هَهُنَا
sentences.tr: wa-in tamahhalta wa-amʿanta al-naẓara fīmā aḥkīhi laka ʿarafta qaṣdī alladhī qaṣadtuhu wa-in ʿajilta bi-qatlī fa-lā yaḥṣulu fī yadika shayʾun wa-namūtu jamīʿan hahunā
sentences.l: And if you-take-your-time and look-deeply in what I-relate to-you, you-will-know my purpose which I-purposed; and if you-hasten with my killing, then nothing comes-about in your hand, and we-die together here.
sentences.i: If you take your time and weigh carefully what I tell you, you will understand what I had in mind; but if you are quick to kill me, you will gain nothing by it, and we shall both die here together.”
sentences.n: amʿana al-naẓar fī, “to look closely into, consider carefully”. qaṣdī alladhī qaṣadtuhu, “my purpose which I purposed”, the noun and its own verb together for emphasis. hahunā, “here”, as the print writes it; the hamza in شيء is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الذِّئْبُ أَيُّهَا الْخَادِعُ الْمَاكِرُ وَمَا الَّذِى تَرْجُوهُ مِنْ سَلَامَتِي وَسَلَامَتِكَ حَتَّى تَسْأَلَنِي التَّمَهُّلَ عَلَيْكَ فَأَعْلِمْنِي وَأَخْبِرْنِي بِقَصْدِكَ الَّذِى قَصَدْتَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-dhiʾbu ayyuhā al-khādiʿu al-mākiru wa-mā alladhī tarjūhu min salāmatī wa-salāmatika ḥattā tasʾalanī al-tamahhula ʿalayka fa-aʿlimnī wa-akhbirnī bi-qaṣdika alladhī qaṣadtahu
sentences.l: And the wolf said to him: O deceiver, the crafty-one, and what (is it) which you-hope-for from my safety and your safety, so-that you-ask-me (for) the going-slowly with-you? So inform-me and tell-me of your-purpose which you-purposed.
sentences.i: The wolf said to him, “You cunning deceiver, what do you hope to gain from my safety and yours, that you ask me to go easy with you? Tell me plainly what you are after.”
sentences.n: tamahhul ʿalā, “going slowly with, bearing patiently with (someone)”. qaṣdika alladhī qaṣadtahu, “your purpose that you purposed”: a noun followed by its own verb, a common emphatic figure, which the fox echoes in his reply.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الثَّعْلَبُ أَمَّا قَصْدِي الَّذِى قَصَدْتُهُ فَمَا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تُحْسِنَ عَلَيْهِ مُجَازَاتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-thaʿlabu ammā qaṣdī alladhī qaṣadtuhu fa-mā yanbaghī an tuḥsina ʿalayhi mujāzātī
sentences.l: And the fox said to him: As for my-purpose which I-purposed, (it is) what it-befits that you-make-good for-it my-requital,
sentences.i: The fox answered, “As for my purpose, it is one for which you ought to reward me handsomely,
sentences.n: ammā … fa-, “as for … then”: the fa- opens the answer. fa-mā yanbaghī is best taken as “it is (a thing) for which it is fitting that …”, with mā meaning “that which”; read as a negative, “it is not fitting”, it would have the fox refuse any reward, which the “because” that follows does not support. aḥsana al-mujāzāta, “to make a fine requital”.

sentences.t: لِأَنِّي لَمَّا سَمِعْتُ مَا وَعَدْتَ مِنْ نَفْسِكَ وَاعْتِرَافَكَ بِمَا سَلَفَ مِنْكَ وَتَلَهُّفَكَ عَلَى مَافَاتَكَ مِنَ الْقُوَّةِ وَفِعْلِ الْخَيْرِ وَسَمِعْتُ مَا نَذَرْتَهُ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ إِنْ نَجَوْتَ مِمَّا أَنْتَ فِيهِ مِنْ كَفِّ الْأَذَى عَنِ الْأَصْحَابِ وَغَيْرِهِمْ وَتَرْكِكَ أَكْلَ الْعِنَبِ وَسَائِرِ الْفَوَاكِهِ وَلُزُومِكَ الْخُشُوعَ وَتَقْلِيمِ أَظْفَارِكَ وَتَكْسِيرِ أَنْيَابِكَ وَلُبْسِ الصُّوفِ وَتَقْرِيبِكَ الْقُرْبَانَ لِلّٰهِ تَعَالَى أَخَذَتْنِي الشَّفَقَةُ عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: li-annī lammā samiʿtu mā waʿadta min nafsika wa-iʿtirāfaka bi-mā salafa minka wa-talahhufaka ʿalā mā fātaka mina al-quwwati wa-fiʿli al-khayri wa-samiʿtu mā nadhartahu ʿalā nafsika in najawta mimmā anta fīhi min kaffi al-adhā ʿani al-aṣḥābi wa-ghayrihim wa-tarkika akla al-ʿinabi wa-sāʾiri al-fawākihi wa-luzūmika al-khushūʿa wa-taqlīmi aẓfārika wa-taksīri anyābika wa-lubsi al-ṣūfi wa-taqrībika al-qurbāna li-allāhi taʿālā akhadhatnī al-shafaqatu ʿalayka
sentences.l: because I, when I-heard what you-promised of yourself, and your-confessing of what went-before from-you, and your-lamenting over what escaped-you of strength and doing of good, and I-heard what you-vowed upon yourself if you-escaped from what you (are) in-it: of holding-back the harm from the companions and others, and your-leaving the eating of grapes and the rest of the fruits, and your-keeping-to humility, and paring your-claws, and breaking your-fangs, and wearing of wool, and your-bringing-near the offering to God the Exalted, — pity for-you took-me.
sentences.i: for when I heard what you promised on your own account, how you confessed your past deeds and lamented the strength and the good works you had let slip, and when I heard the vows you made should you be saved from your plight, to keep from harming your companions and everyone else, to give up eating grapes and every other fruit, to cling to humility, to pare your claws and break your fangs, to wear wool and to offer sacrifice to God the Exalted, I was seized with pity for you.
sentences.n: The fox recites back the wolf's vows in the pit. The verbal nouns kaff, tark, luzūm, taqlīm, taksīr, lubs and taqrīb all hang on the one min, “consisting of”. taqrīb al-qurbān, “bringing near the thing brought near”: verb and noun from the same root q-r-b, the offering being what is brought near to God. The print runs mā fātaka together as مافاتك; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ خَيْرَ الْقَوْلِ أَصْدَقُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-inna khayra al-qawli aṣdaquhu
sentences.l: For the best of speech (is) its-truest.
sentences.i: For the best of words is the truest.
sentences.n: A saying. aṣdaquhu, “its most truthful”: the elative with a pronoun referring back to al-qawl. With it the fox prefaces an admission to his own discredit.

sentences.t: مَعَ أَنِّي كُنْتُ عَلَى هَلَاكِكَ حَرِيصًا فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ مِنْكَ تَوْبَتَكَ وَمَا نَذَرْتَهُ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ إِنْ نَجَّاكَ اللَّهُ لَزِمَنِي لَكَ الْخَلَاصُ مِمَّا أَنْتَ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: maʿa annī kuntu ʿalā halākika ḥarīṣan fa-lammā samiʿtu minka tawbataka wa-mā nadhartahu ʿalā nafsika in najjāka allāhu lazimanī laka al-khalāṣu mimmā anta fīhi
sentences.l: Although I was for your-destruction eager; but when I-heard from-you your-repentance and what you-vowed upon yourself if God saved-you, there-became-binding-on-me for-you the deliverance from what you (are) in-it.
sentences.i: I had been eager for your ruin, I confess; but when I heard your repentance from your own lips, and the vows you made should God save you, I felt bound to deliver you from your plight.
sentences.n: maʿa anna, “in spite of the fact that”. lazimanī, “it became binding on me”: the thing owed, al-khalāṣ, is the subject, so “I was obliged to deliver you”.

sentences.t: فَأَدْلَيْتُ إِلَيْكَ ذَنَبِي لِكَيْمَا تَتَعَلَّقَ بِهِ وَتَنْجُوَ
sentences.tr: fa-adlaytu ilayka dhanabī li-kaymā tataʿallaqa bihi wa-tanjuwa
sentences.l: So I-let-down to-you my-tail so-that you-might-hang onto-it and be-saved.
sentences.i: So I let my tail down to you, that you might catch hold of it and be saved.
sentences.n: dhanab, “tail”, is written with the same letters as dhanb, “sin”. li-kaymā, “in order that”, a strengthened kay, takes the subjunctive: tataʿallaqa, tanjuwa.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ تَتْرُكِ الْحَالَةَ الَّتِي أَنْتَ عَلَيْهَا مِنَ الْعُنْفِ وَالشِّدَّةِ وَلَمْ تَلْتَمِسِ النَّجَاةَ وَالسَّلَامَةَ لِنَفْسِكَ بِالرِّفْقِ بَلْ جَذَبْتَنِي جَذْبَةً ظَنَنْتُ مِنْهَا أَنَّ رُوحِي قَدْ خَرَجَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lam tatruki al-ḥālata allatī anta ʿalayhā mina al-ʿunfi wa-al-shiddati wa-lam taltamisi al-najāta wa-al-salāmata li-nafsika bi-al-rifqi bal jadhabtanī jadhbatan ẓanantu minhā anna rūḥī qad kharajat
sentences.l: But you-did-not leave the state which you (are) upon-it, of violence and harshness, and you-did-not seek the escape and the safety for yourself by gentleness; rather you-pulled-me a pull from which I-thought that my-soul had gone-out.
sentences.i: But you would not give up your old ways of violence and harshness, nor seek escape and safety for yourself by gentle means; instead you gave me such a yank that I thought my soul had left my body.
sentences.n: jadhabtanī jadhbatan, a verb with its own noun of a single act (the pattern faʿla): “you pulled me one pull”, that is, one mighty pull.

sentences.t: فَصِرْتُ أَنَا وَأَنْتَ فِي مَنْزِلَةِ الْهَلَاكِ وَالْمَوْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣirtu anā wa-anta fī manzilati al-halāki wa-al-mawti
sentences.l: So I-came-to-be, I and you, in the station of destruction and death.
sentences.i: And so you and I alike came to the very brink of ruin and death.
sentences.n: ṣirtu anā wa-anta: the verb agrees with “I”, and anā wa-anta, “I and you”, is added after it to bring in the second subject.

sentences.t: وَمَا يُنْجِينِي وَأَنْتَ إِلَّا شَيْءٌ إِنْ قَبِلْتَهُ مِنِّي خَلَصْتُ أَنَا وَأَنْتَ
sentences.tr: wa-mā yunjīnī wa-anta illā shayʾun in qabiltahu minnī khalaṣtu anā wa-anta
sentences.l: And nothing saves-me and you except a thing (which), if you-accept-it from-me, I-am-delivered, I and you.
sentences.i: Nothing can save us both but one thing: if you will take it from me, you and I will both go free.
sentences.n: yunjīnī wa-anta, “saves me and you”: the free pronoun anta is joined to the attached -nī, a loose construction where Classical Arabic would say yunjīnī wa-iyyāka.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ يَجِبُ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَفِيَ بِمَانَذَرْتَهُ وَأَكُونَ رَفِيقَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika yajibu ʿalayka an tafiya bi-mā nadhartahu wa-akūna rafīqaka
sentences.l: And after that it-is-incumbent upon-you that you-fulfil what you-vowed, and (that) I-be your-companion.
sentences.i: After that you must fulfil your vow, and I shall be your companion.”
sentences.n: wafā bi-, “to keep (a promise), fulfil (a vow)”: the verb takes what is kept with bi-. akūna is subjunctive, still governed by an. The print runs bi-mā nadhartahu together as بمانذرته; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الذِّئْبُ وَمَا الَّذِي أَقْبَلُهُ مِنْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-dhiʾbu wa-mā alladhī aqbaluhu minka
sentences.l: And the wolf said to him: And what (is it) which I-accept from-you?
sentences.i: “And what is it I am to take from you?” asked the wolf.

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهُ الثَّعْلَبُ تَنْهَضُ قَائِمًا ثُمَّ اَعْلُو أَنَا فَوْقَ رَأْسِكَ حَتَّى أُسَاوِيَ قَرِيبَ ظَهْرِ الْأَرْضِ فَأَهْمِزَ فَأَصِيرَ فَوْقَهَا وَأَخْرُجُ أَنَا وَآتِيكَ بِمَا تَتَعَلَّقُ بِهِ وَتَخْلُصُ أَنْتَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: qāla lahu al-thaʿlabu tanhaḍu qāʾiman thumma aʿlū anā fawqa raʾsika ḥattā usāwiya qarība ẓahri al-arḍi fa-ahmiza fa-aṣīra fawqahā wa-akhruju anā wa-ātīka bi-mā tataʿallaqu bihi wa-takhluṣu anta baʿda dhālika
sentences.l: The fox said to him: You-rise standing, then I-mount, I, above your-head, until I-am-level-with near the back of the earth; then I-spring and come-to-be upon-it; and I-go-out, I, and bring-you what you-hang onto-it, and you-are-delivered, you, after that.
sentences.i: The fox said, “You stand up straight, and I will climb on top of your head until I am nearly level with the ground above; then I will spring and be up on it. I will go off and fetch you something to hold on to, and after that you will get free.”
sentences.n: tanhaḍu, an indicative used as a gentle instruction: “you rise”. The fatḥa on اَعْلُو is the print's own, which writes no hamza on the alif. ẓahr al-arḍ, “the back of the earth”, is its surface. hamaza is properly “to press, to goad”; here it must mean “push off, spring up”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الذِّئْبُ لَسْتُ بِقَوْلِكَ وَاثِقًا لِأَنَّ الْحُكَمَاءَ قَالُوا مَنِ اسْتَعْمَلَ الثِّقَةَ فِي مَوْضِعِ الْحِقْدِ كَانَ مُخْطِئًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-dhiʾbu lastu bi-qawlika wāthiqan li-anna al-ḥukamāʾa qālū mani istaʿmala al-thiqata fī mawḍiʿi al-ḥiqdi kāna mukhṭiʾan
sentences.l: And the wolf said to him: I-am-not in your-word trusting, because the wise-ones said: Whoever employs trust in the place of rancour is mistaken,
sentences.i: The wolf answered, “I have no faith in your word. The sages have said: He who puts trust where enmity belongs is in error;
sentences.n: wathiqa bi-, “to trust in”: bi- names what is trusted, and bi-qawlika is put before wāthiqan for emphasis. ḥiqd, “rancour, a grudge nursed in secret”.

sentences.t: وَمَنْ وَثِقَ بِغَيْرِ ثِقَةٍ كَانَ مَغْرُورًا وَمَنْ جَرَّبَ الْمُجَرَّبَ حَلَّتْ بِهِ النَّدَامَةُ وَذَهَبَتْ أَيَّامُهُ ضَيَاعًا
sentences.tr: wa-man wathiqa bi-ghayri thiqatin kāna maghrūran wa-man jarraba al-mujarraba ḥallat bihi al-nadāmatu wa-dhahabat ayyāmuhu ḍayāʿan
sentences.l: and whoever trusts without trustworthiness is deluded; and whoever tests the (already-)tested, remorse alights on-him and his-days go (in) loss.
sentences.i: he who trusts without good ground is a dupe; and he who puts to the test what has already been tested will be visited by remorse and see his days run to waste.
sentences.n: “Whoever tests the tested, remorse comes upon him” is a well-known proverb: once a man has proved false, do not try him again. ḥalla bi-, “to descend upon, befall”. ḍayāʿan, “in loss, to waste”, an accusative of manner.

sentences.t: وَمَنْ لَمْ يُفَرِّقْ بَيْنَ الْحَالَاتِ فَيُعْطِيَ كُلَّ حَالَةٍ حَظَّهَا بَلْ حَمَلَ الْأَشْيَاءَ كُلَّهَا عَلَى حَالَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ قَلَّ حَظُّهُ وَكَثُرَتْ مَصَائِبُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-man lam yufarriq bayna al-ḥālāti fa-yuʿṭiya kulla ḥālatin ḥaẓẓahā bal ḥamala al-ashyāʾa kullahā ʿalā ḥālatin wāḥidatin qalla ḥaẓẓuhu wa-kathurat maṣāʾibuhu
sentences.l: And whoever does-not distinguish between the conditions, so-as-to-give each condition its-share, but carries the things, all-of-them, on one condition, his-luck becomes-little and his-misfortunes become-many.
sentences.i: And he who cannot tell one case from another and give each its due, but treats all things alike, will have little luck and many misfortunes.
sentences.n: ḥaẓẓ means both “due share” and “good fortune”, and the maxim plays on the two: whoever denies each case its ḥaẓẓ loses his own. fa-yuʿṭiya, subjunctive after fa- following a negative: “so as to give”.

sentences.t: وَمَا أَحْسَنَ قَوْلَ الشَّاعِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā aḥsana qawla al-shāʿiri
sentences.l: And how fine (is) the saying of the poet:
sentences.i: How well the poet puts it:

sentences.t:
لَا يَكُنْ ظَنُّكَ اِلَّا سَيِّأً * اِنَّ سُوْءَ الظَّنّ مِنْ اَقْوَى الْفِطَنْ
مَارُمِي الْاِنْسَانُ فِي مَهْلِكَةٍ * مِثْل فِعْلِ الْخَيْرِ وَالظَّنِّ الْحَسَنْ
sentences.tr:
lā yakun ẓannuka illā sayyiʾan * inna sūʾa al-ẓanni min aqwā al-fiṭan
mā rumiya al-insānu fī mahlakatin * mithla fiʿli al-khayri wa-al-ẓanni al-ḥasan
sentences.l:
Let your-thought not be except evil; * truly ill of thought (is) among the strongest of the shrewdnesses.
Man is-not cast into a perilous-place * like the doing of good and the good thought.
sentences.i:
Think nothing but ill of anyone: * suspicion is the surest kind of wit.
Nothing casts a man into peril * like doing good and thinking well.
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own. sūʾ al-ẓann, “bad opinion”, is the stock phrase for suspicion, as ḥusn al-ẓann is for trust. sayyiʾan, “bad”, is printed with its hamza on the alif (سَيِّأً) rather than the usual سيّئًا. fiṭan, plural of fiṭna, “shrewdness”. mahlaka, “a place of perdition”. The rhyme words al-fiṭan and al-ḥasan are pointed with sukūn, as they are said at the end of a line. The print runs mā rumiya together as مَارُمِي; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: وَقَوْلَ الْآخَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-qawla al-ākhari
sentences.l: And the saying of the other:
sentences.i: And another:
sentences.n: qawla is still governed by mā aḥsana above: “and (how fine is) the saying of another”.

sentences.t:
اِلْزَمْ يَقِينَكَ سُوْءَ الظَّنِّ تَنْجُ بِهِ * مَنْ عَاشَ مُسْتَيْقِظاً قَلَّتْ مَصَائِبُهُ
وَالْقِ الْعَدُوَّ بِوَجْهٍ بَاسِمٍ طَلِقٍ * وَانْصِبْ لَهُ فِى الْحَشَى جَيْشاً يُحَارِبُهُ
sentences.tr:
ilzam yaqīnaka sūʾa al-ẓanni tanju bihi * man ʿāsha mustayqiẓan qallat maṣāʾibuhu
wa-alqi al-ʿaduwwa bi-wajhin bāsimin ṭaliqin * wa-inṣib lahu fī al-ḥashā jayshan yuḥāribuhu
sentences.l:
Hold-fast, (as) your-certainty, to ill-thought: you-will-be-saved by-it; * whoever lives wakeful, his-misfortunes become-few.
And meet the enemy with a face smiling, cheerful, * and set-up for-him in the entrails an army (that) fights-him.
sentences.i:
Make suspicion your certainty and it will save you: * whoever lives wide awake has fewer troubles.
Meet your enemy with a smiling, open face, * and in your heart muster an army to fight him.
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own. yaqīnaka, “your certainty”, stands in the accusative beside sūʾa al-ẓanni, as if the verb took two objects: “hold to suspicion as your certainty”. tanju, jussive, answers the command: “(do so) and you will be saved”. The print writes وَالْقِ without the hamza of alqi, “meet” (literally “throw yourself toward”). al-ḥashā, “the entrails”, the inward parts where feeling is hidden.

sentences.t: وَقَوْلَ الْآخَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-qawla al-ākhari
sentences.l: And the saying of the other:
sentences.i: And another:

sentences.t:
اَعْدَى عَدُوِّكَ اَدْنَى مَنْ وَثِقْتَ بِهِ * فَحَاذِرِ النَّاسَ وَاصْحَبْهُمْ عَلَى دَخَلِ
وَحُسْنُ ظَنِّكَ بِالْاَيَّامِ مُعْجِزَةٌ * فَظُنَّ شَرّاً وَكُنْ مِنْهَا عَلَى وَجَلِ
sentences.tr:
aʿdā ʿaduwwika adnā man wathiqta bihi * fa-ḥādhiri al-nāsa wa-iṣḥabhum ʿalā dakhali
wa-ḥusnu ẓannika bi-al-ayyāmi muʿjizatun * fa-ẓunna sharran wa-kun minhā ʿalā wajali
sentences.l:
The most-hostile of your-enemies (is) the nearest of whom you-trusted in-him; * so beware-of the people and keep-company-with-them upon mistrust.
And your good-thought of the days (is) a miracle; * so think evil, and be of-them in fear.
sentences.i:
Your worst enemy is the one you trust most closely: * be wary of people, and keep their company with a guarded heart.
To think well of the times would be a wonder: * think the worst, and stand in fear of them.”
sentences.n: Two lines from the Lāmiyyat al-ʿAjam of al-Ṭughrāʾī (d. c. 1121), a celebrated ode on the faithlessness of the age. The pointing is the print's own. dakhal, “a hidden flaw, inner mistrust”: ʿalā dakhal, “with reserve”. The print points muʿjizatun, “a miracle”, a thing past all expectation; the line is also read maʿjazatun, “a mark of helplessness”. The rhyme words dakhali and wajali keep their final kasra for the rhyme.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الثَّعْلَبُ إِنَّ سُوءَ الظَّنِّ لَيْسَ بِمَحْمُودٍ فِي كُلِّ حَالٍ وَحُسْنَ الظَّنِّ مِنْ شِيَمِ الْكُمَّالِ وَعَاقِبَتُهُ النَّجَاةُ مِنَ الْأَهْوَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-thaʿlabu inna sūʾa al-ẓanni laysa bi-maḥmūdin fī kulli ḥālin wa-ḥusna al-ẓanni min shiyami al-kummāli wa-ʿāqibatuhu al-najātu mina al-ahwāli
sentences.l: And the fox said to him: Truly ill-thought is not praiseworthy in every state; and good-thought (is) of the traits of the perfect-ones, and its-outcome (is) the escape from the terrors.
sentences.i: The fox said, “Suspicion is not to be praised in every case. To think well of others is a trait of the perfect, and its end is deliverance from terrors.
sentences.n: The print has فقالت, a misprint for فقال, corrected here: the fox is masculine throughout. The reply is in rhymed prose: ḥāl, kummāl, ahwāl. kummāl, plural of kāmil, “the perfect, the accomplished”; shiyam, plural of shīma, “inborn trait”.

sentences.t: وَيَنْبَغِي لَكَ أَيُّهَا الذِّئْبُ أَنْ تَعْمَلَ حِيلَةً عَلَى النَّجَاةِ مِمَّا أَنْتَ فِيهِ وَنَسْلَمُ جَمِيعًا خَيْرٌ مِنْ مَوْتِنَا
sentences.tr: wa-yanbaghī laka ayyuhā al-dhiʾbu an taʿmala ḥīlatan ʿalā al-najāti mimmā anta fīhi wa-naslamu jamīʿan khayrun min mawtinā
sentences.l: And it-befits you, O wolf, that you-work a stratagem toward the escape from what you (are) in-it; and (that) we-are-safe together (is) better than our-dying.
sentences.i: You ought, wolf, to find some stratagem to escape your plight. For us both to come off safe is better than for us both to die.
sentences.n: wa-naslamu jamīʿan khayrun min mawtinā: a bare verb serves as the subject, “(that) we are safe together is better than our dying”, as in the proverb tasmaʿu bi-al-muʿaydiyyi khayrun min an tarāhu, “(that) you hear of the Muʿaydī is better than that you see him”. Classical Arabic would write an naslama.

sentences.t: فَارْجِعْ عَنْ سُوءِ الظَّنِّ وَالْحِقْدِ لِأَنَّكَ إِنْ أَحْسَنْتَ الظَّنَّ فَالْأَمْرُ عَلَى وَجْهَيْنِ إِمَّا أَنْ آتِيَكَ بِمَا تَتَعَلَّقُ بِهِ وَتَنْجُو مِمَّا أَنْتَ فِيهِ وَإِمَّا أَنْ أَغُلَّ رَبَّكَ فَأَخْلُصَ وَأَدَعَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-irjiʿ ʿan sūʾi al-ẓanni wa-al-ḥiqdi li-annaka in aḥsanta al-ẓanna fa-al-amru ʿalā wajhayni immā an ātiyaka bi-mā tataʿallaqu bihi wa-tanjū mimmā anta fīhi wa-immā an aghulla rabbaka fa-akhluṣa wa-adaʿaka
sentences.l: So turn-back from ill-thought and rancour; because you, if you-think-well, then the matter (is) on two faces: either that I-bring-you what you-hang onto-it and you-escape from what you (are) in-it, or that I [betray you], and get-free, and leave-you.
sentences.i: So put away your suspicion and your rancour. If you think well of me, it can go only one of two ways: either I bring you something to hold on to and you escape your plight, or I play you false, get away and leave you behind.
sentences.n: The print has اغل ربك, which as it stands would read aghulla rabbaka, “I defraud your Lord”, and makes no sense here. The sense needed is “betray you”, and the words are probably a corruption of اغدر بك, aghdira bika; the translation follows that sense, the pointing the printed letters. aḥsana al-ẓanna, “to think well (of someone)”. immā … wa-immā, “either … or”.

sentences.t: وَهَذَا مِمَّا لَا يُمْكِنُ فَإِنِّي لَا آمَنُ أَنْ أُبْتَلَي بِشَيْءٍ مِمَّا ابْتُلِيتَ بِهِ فَيَكُونَ ذَلِكَ عُقُوبَةَ الْغَدْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā mimmā lā yumkinu fa-innī lā āmanu an ubtalā bi-shayʾin mimmā ubtulīta bihi fa-yakūna dhālika ʿuqūbata al-ghadri
sentences.l: And this (is) of what is-not possible; for I do-not feel-safe (from) that I-be-afflicted with a thing of what you-were-afflicted with-it, and that be the punishment of treachery.
sentences.i: But that cannot be; for I should never feel safe from being struck by some such affliction as has struck you, as the punishment for treachery.
sentences.n: lā āmanu an, “I am not safe from (the risk) that …”. ubtuliya bi-, “to be tried, afflicted with”, passive of ibtalā. The print spells ubtalā with a final ي (ابتلي).

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قِيلَ فِى الْأَمْثَالِ الْوَفَاءُ مَلِيحٌ وَالْغَدْرُ قَبِيحٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qad qīla fī al-amthāli al-wafāʾu malīḥun wa-al-ghadru qabīḥun
sentences.l: And it-has-been-said in the proverbs: Faithfulness (is) comely, and treachery (is) ugly.
sentences.i: As the proverb has it, keeping faith is fair and treachery foul.
sentences.n: A rhymed saying, malīḥ / qabīḥ.

sentences.t: فَيَنْبَغِي أَنْ تَثِقَ بِي فَإِنِّي لَمْ أَكُنْ جَاهِلًا بِحَوَادِثِ الدَّهْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-yanbaghī an tathiqa bī fa-innī lam akun jāhilan bi-ḥawādithi al-dahri
sentences.l: So it-befits that you-trust in-me, for I have-not-been ignorant of the happenings of fate.
sentences.i: So you ought to trust me: I am no stranger to the turns of fortune.
sentences.n: ḥawādith al-dahr, “the happenings of time”: the blows of fortune.

sentences.t: فَلَا تُؤَخِّرْ حِيلَةَ خَلَاصِنَا فَالْأَمْرُ أَضْيَقُ مِنْ أَنْ نُطِيلَ فِيهِ الْكَلَامَ
sentences.tr: fa-lā tuʾakhkhir ḥīlata khalāṣinā fa-al-amru aḍyaqu min an nuṭīla fīhi al-kalāma
sentences.l: So do-not delay the stratagem of our-deliverance; for the matter (is) narrower than that we-lengthen in-it the talk.
sentences.i: Do not put off the means of our escape: the matter is too pressing for long speeches.”
sentences.n: aḍyaqu min an, “narrower than that …”: the comparative with min an gives “too … to”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الذِّئْبُ إِنَّ مَعَ قِلَّةِ ثِقَتِي بِوَفَائِكَ قَدْ عَرَفْتُ مَافِي خَاطِرِكَ مِنْ أَنَّكَ أَرَدْتَ خَلَاصِي لَمَّا سَمِعْتَ مِنْ تَوْبَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-dhiʾbu inna maʿa qillati thiqatī bi-wafāʾika qad ʿaraftu mā fī khāṭirika min annaka aradta khalāṣī lammā samiʿta min tawbatī
sentences.l: And the wolf said: Truly, with the littleness of my-trust in your-faithfulness, I-have known what (is) in your-mind: that you wanted my-deliverance when you-heard of my-repentance.
sentences.i: The wolf said, “Little as I trust your good faith, I have understood what is in your mind: that you meant to save me when you heard of my repentance.
sentences.n: inna here has no noun after it, and the sentence goes on as if it had said innī, “I”: a loose use of inna as a mere opener. khāṭir, “mind, what passes through the mind”. The print runs mā fī together as مافي; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي إِنْ كَانَ مُحِقًّا فِيمَا زَعَمَ فَإِنَّهُ اسْتَدْرَكَ مَا انْسَلَّ وَإِنْ كَانَ مُبْطِلًا فَجَزَاؤُهُ عَلَى رَبِّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu fī nafsī in kāna muḥiqqan fīmā zaʿama fa-innahu istadraka mā insalla wa-in kāna mubṭilan fa-jazāʾuhu ʿalā rabbihi
sentences.l: So I-said in myself: If he-is in-the-right in what he-claimed, then he has-made-good what slipped-away; and if he-is in-the-wrong, then his-requital (is) upon his-Lord.
sentences.i: So I said to myself: If he is honest in what he claims, he has made good what had slipped away; and if he is false, his Lord will repay him.
sentences.n: The phrase استدرك ما انسل, “he has made good what slipped away”, is doubtful: it is read here as the fox repairing his earlier lapse, but the text may be corrupt, and a reading such as استدرك ما اسلف, “he has made amends for what he did before”, is possible. muḥiqq / mubṭil, “in the right / in the wrong”, a standing pair. ʿalā rabbihi, “(falls) upon his Lord”: God will settle the account.

sentences.t: وَهَا أَنَا أَقْبَلُ مِنْكَ مَا أَشَرْتَ بِهِ عَلَيَّ فَإِنْ غَدَرْتَ بِي كَانَ الْغَدْرُ سَبَبًا لِهَلَاكِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-hā anā aqbalu minka mā asharta bihi ʿalayya fa-in ghadarta bī kāna al-ghadru sababan li-halākika
sentences.l: And here I (am) accepting from-you what you-advised with-it upon-me; and if you-betray me, the treachery will-be a cause for your-destruction.
sentences.i: Well then, I accept the plan you have put to me; and if you betray me, your treachery will be your undoing.”
sentences.n: ashāra ʿalayhi bi-, “to advise someone (ʿalā) to do something (bi-)”. ghadara bi-, “to betray (someone)”: the verb takes its object with bi-. The shadda in عليّ is the print's own.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الذِّئْبَ انْتَصَبَ قَائِمًا فِى الْحُفْرَةِ وَأَخَذَ الثَّعْلَبَ عَلَى أَكْتَافِهِ حَتَّى سَاوَى بِهِ ظَاهِرَ الْأَرْضِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-dhiʾba intaṣaba qāʾiman fī al-ḥufrati wa-akhadha al-thaʿlaba ʿalā aktāfihi ḥattā sāwā bihi ẓāhira al-arḍi
sentences.l: Then the wolf stood-erect standing in the pit and took the fox on his-shoulders until he-made-level with-him the surface of the earth.
sentences.i: Then the wolf stood upright in the pit and took the fox on his shoulders, until he had raised him level with the ground above.
sentences.n: aktāf, plural of katif, “shoulder”: the plural for a pair is common in the Nights. sāwā bihi, “brought level”: bi- marks what is brought level with the ground.

sentences.t: فَقَفَزَ الثَّعْلَبُ عَنْ أَكْتَافِ الذِّئْبِ فَصَارَ عَلَى وَجْهِ الْأَرْضِ
sentences.tr: fa-qafaza al-thaʿlabu ʿan aktāfi al-dhiʾbi fa-ṣāra ʿalā wajhi al-arḍi
sentences.l: And the fox leapt from the shoulders of the wolf and came-to-be on the face of the earth.
sentences.i: The fox leapt from the wolf's shoulders and was up on the open ground.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا صَارَ خَارِجَ الْحُفْرَةِ وَقَعَ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṣāra khārija al-ḥufrati waqaʿa maghshiyyan ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And when he-was outside the pit, he-fell covered-over upon-him.
sentences.i: Once clear of the pit, he fell down in a swoon.
sentences.n: maghshiyyan ʿalayhi, “fainted”, literally “covered over upon him”: the stock expression for losing consciousness.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الذِّئْبُ يَا خَلِيلِي لَاتَغْفُلْ عَنْ أَمْرِي وَلَاتُؤَخِّرْ خَلَاصِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-dhiʾbu yā khalīlī lā taghful ʿan amrī wa-lā tuʾakhkhir khalāṣī
sentences.l: And the wolf said to him: O my-friend, do-not be-heedless of my-affair, and do-not delay my-deliverance.
sentences.i: “My dear friend,” said the wolf, “do not forget me, and do not be slow to get me out.”
sentences.n: The print runs lā together with the verb in لاتغفل and ولاتؤخر; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ الثَّعْلَبُ وَقَهْقَهَ وَقَالَ أَيُّهَا الْمَغْرُورُ لَمْ يُوقِعْنِي فِي يَدَيْكَ إِلَّاعُقُوبَةُ الْمَزْحِ مَعَكَ وَالسُّخْرِيَّةِ بِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika al-thaʿlabu wa-qahqaha wa-qāla ayyuhā al-maghrūru lam yūqiʿnī fī yadayka illā ʿuqūbatu al-mazḥi maʿaka wa-al-sukhriyyati bika
sentences.l: And the fox laughed and guffawed and said: O deluded-one, nothing cast-me into your-two-hands except the punishment of the joking with-you and the mocking at-you.
sentences.i: The fox laughed aloud and said, “You fool! Nothing put me into your hands but the punishment for joking with you and making mock of you.
sentences.n: qahqaha, “to laugh out loud”, an imitative word. sakhira bi-, “to mock (someone)”: the noun keeps the verb's bi-. The print runs illā together with ʿuqūbatu as الاعقوبة; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: وَذَلِكَ أَنِّي لَمَّا سَمِعْتُ تَوْبَتَكَ اسْتَخَفَّنِي الطَّرَبُ وَالْفَرَحُ فَنَطَّيْتُ وَطَرِبْتُ وَرَقَصْتُ فَتَدَلَّى ذَنَبِي فِى الْحُفْرَةِ فَجَذَبْتَنِي فَوَقَعْتُ عِنْدَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-dhālika annī lammā samiʿtu tawbataka istakhaffanī al-ṭarabu wa-al-faraḥu fa-naṭṭaytu wa-ṭaribtu wa-raqaṣtu fa-tadallā dhanabī fī al-ḥufrati fa-jadhabtanī fa-waqaʿtu ʿindaka
sentences.l: And that (is) that I, when I-heard your-repentance, rapture and joy made-me-light, so I-jumped and was-transported and danced; and my-tail dangled into the pit, and you-pulled-me, and I-fell beside-you.
sentences.i: For when I heard of your repentance, I was so carried away with delight and glee that I leapt and capered and danced; my tail dangled into the pit, you pulled me in, and down I fell beside you.
sentences.n: fa-naṭṭaytu, “I jumped”: from the spoken verb naṭṭ / naṭṭā, “to leap”, not a Classical word, so the pointing is a guess at the spoken form. istakhaffa, “to make light, carry away”: joy lifted him off his feet. wa-dhālika anna, “and that is because”, introducing an explanation.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنْقَذَنِى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى مِنْكَ فَمَا لِي لَاأَكُونُ عَوْنًا عَلَى هَلَاكِكَ لِأَنَّكَ مِنْ حِزْبِ الشَّيْطَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma anqadhanī allāhu taʿālā minka fa-mā lī lā akūnu ʿawnan ʿalā halākika li-annaka min ḥizbi al-shayṭāni
sentences.l: Then God the Exalted rescued-me from-you; so what (is) to-me (that) I-be-not a help toward your-destruction? For you (are) of the party of Satan.
sentences.i: Then God the Exalted rescued me from you. Why then should I not lend a hand to your ruin? You are of the party of Satan.
sentences.n: fa-mā lī lā akūnu, “what is with me that I should not be …”, that is, “why should I not be …”. ḥizb al-shayṭān, “the party of Satan”, is a Qurʾānic phrase (58:19). The print runs lā akūnu together as لااكون; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: وَإِنِّي رَأَيْتُ الْبَارِحَةَ فِي مَنَامِي أَنِّي أَرْقُصُ فِي عُرْسِكَ فَقَصَصْتُ الرُّؤْيَا عَلَى مُعَبِّرٍ فَقَالَ لِي إِنَّكَ تَقَعُ فِي وَرْطَةٍ وَتَنْجُو مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-innī raʾaytu al-bāriḥata fī manāmī annī arquṣu fī ʿursika fa-qaṣaṣtu al-ruʾyā ʿalā muʿabbirin fa-qāla lī innaka taqaʿu fī warṭatin wa-tanjū minhā
sentences.l: And I saw last-night in my-sleep that I (was) dancing at your-wedding; so I-related the vision to an interpreter, and he-said to-me: You-will-fall into a predicament and escape from-it.
sentences.i: Last night I dreamed I was dancing at your wedding. I told the dream to an interpreter, and he said to me, ‘You will fall into a tight spot and come out of it.’
sentences.n: muʿabbir, “an interpreter of dreams”, from ʿabbara al-ruʾyā, “to interpret a dream”. warṭa, “a quagmire, a scrape”. al-bāriḥa, “last night”.

sentences.t: فَعَلِمْتُ أَنَّ وُقُوعِي فِي يَدِكَ وَنَجَاتِي هُوَ تَأْوِيلُ رُؤْيَايَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿalimtu anna wuqūʿī fī yadika wa-najātī huwa taʾwīlu ruʾyāya
sentences.l: So I-knew that my-falling into your-hand and my-escape, it (is) the interpretation of my-vision.
sentences.i: So I knew that falling into your hands and getting free again was the meaning of my dream.
sentences.n: huwa is singular though two things go before it: the fall and the escape are taken together as one event. taʾwīl, “interpretation”, also the coming true of a dream.

sentences.t: وَأَنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَيُّهَا الْمَغْرُورُ الْجَاهِلُ أَنَّنِي عَدُوُّكَ فَكَيْفَ تَطْمَعُ بِقِلَّةِ عَقْلِكَ وَجَهْلِكَ فِي إِنْقَاذِى إِيَّاكَ مَعَ مَا سَمِعْتَ مِنْ غِلَظِ كَلَامِي
sentences.tr: wa-anta taʿlamu ayyuhā al-maghrūru al-jāhilu annanī ʿaduwwuka fa-kayfa taṭmaʿu bi-qillati ʿaqlika wa-jahlika fī inqādhī iyyāka maʿa mā samiʿta min ghilaẓi kalāmī
sentences.l: And you know, O deluded, ignorant-one, that I (am) your-enemy; so how do-you-covet, with the littleness of your-mind and your-ignorance, my-rescuing you, with what you-heard of the coarseness of my-speech?
sentences.i: You know very well, you ignorant dupe, that I am your enemy. How can you be so witless and so foolish as to hope I would rescue you, after the harsh words you have heard from me?
sentences.n: ṭamiʿa fī, “to hope greedily for, to covet”. inqādhī iyyāka, “my rescuing you”: the noun takes its doer as the suffix -ī, so the one rescued stands as the free pronoun iyyāka. bi-qillati ʿaqlika, “with (that is, out of) the littleness of your mind”.

sentences.t: وَكَيْفَ أَسْعَى فِي نَجَاتِكَ وَقَدْ قَالَتِ الْعُلَمَاءُ إِنَّ فِي مَوْتِ الْفَاجِرِ رَاحَةً لِلنَّاسِ وَتَطْهِيرًا لِلْأَرْضِ
sentences.tr: wa-kayfa asʿā fī najātika wa-qad qālati al-ʿulamāʾu inna fī mawti al-fājiri rāḥatan li-al-nāsi wa-taṭhīran li-al-arḍi
sentences.l: And how shall-I-strive in your-escape, when the learned-ones have-said: Truly in the death of the wicked (is) rest for the people and a cleansing for the earth?
sentences.i: And how should I labour to save you, when the learned have said that the death of the wicked brings rest to mankind and cleanses the earth?
sentences.n: saʿā fī, “to work for, strive after”.

sentences.t: وَلَوْلَا مَخَافَةُ أَنْ أَحْتَمِلَ مِنَ الْأَلَمِ فِى الْوَفَاءِ لَكَ مَا هُوَ أَعْظَمُ مِنْ أَلَمِ الْغَدْرِ لَتَدَبَّرْتُ فِي خَلَاصِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-lawlā makhāfatu an aḥtamila mina al-alami fī al-wafāʾi laka mā huwa aʿẓamu min alami al-ghadri la-tadabbartu fī khalāṣika
sentences.l: And were-it-not-for fear that I-should-bear, of pain, in the keeping-faith with-you, what is greater than the pain of treachery, I-would-have-planned for your-deliverance.
sentences.i: Were it not that I fear keeping faith with you would cost me more pain than breaking it, I might have given thought to getting you out.”
sentences.n: lawlā …, la-…, “were it not for …, (then) …”: the la- marks the consequence. The fox stands his own sermon on its head: a moment ago he feared the punishment of treachery; now he fears what keeping faith would cost him.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الذِّئْبُ كَلَامَ الثَّعْلَبِ عَضَّ عَلَى كَفِّهِ نَدَمًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-dhiʾbu kalāma al-thaʿlabi ʿaḍḍa ʿalā kaffihi nadaman
sentences.l: And when the wolf heard the speech of the fox, he-bit on his-paw (in) regret.
sentences.i: When the wolf heard what the fox said, he bit his paw in remorse.
sentences.n: ʿaḍḍa ʿalā kaffihi, “he bit on his hand”, the stock gesture of regret; kaff is the palm, here the wolf's paw. nadaman, an accusative giving the cause: “out of remorse”.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she ceased the speech allowed her.
sentences.n: The print sets the name here as two words, شهر زاد; the spacing is kept.
